front_matter.purpose:
# Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates as an Illinois Assisted Living Establishment / Shared Housing Establishment licensed by the Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH) under the Assisted Living and Shared Housing Act (210 ILCS 9) and the Assisted Living and Shared Housing Establishment Code (77 Ill. Adm. Code 295).

The manual has four aims:

1. **Put the regulatory requirements into daily practice.** Each policy turns a statutory or regulatory requirement into steps that staff can follow. These cover assessment and service planning, staffing and training, medication services, resident contracts, admission and retention, dementia programming, and background checks.
2. **Protect residents.** The policies are meant to support resident safety, dignity, choice and rights, and to keep us from admitting or retaining a resident whose needs we cannot meet.
3. **Show compliance to regulators.** The manual gives IDPH surveyors and application reviewers a written record of how **[AGENCY NAME]** meets each applicable rule.
4. **Reduce enforcement risk.** IDPH may assess civil penalties of up to $5,000 per violation, with each day a separate violation, and up to $3,000 per day for caring for a resident who exceeds the care needs defined in the Act (210 ILCS 9/135). Following these policies helps us avoid such penalties.

**Scope.** The manual applies to all **[AGENCY NAME]** owners, the governing body, the director, employees, contractors and volunteers who work at **[FACILITY NAME / ADDRESS]**. Medicaid payment is available only through the HFS Supportive Living Program (89 Ill. Adm. Code 146). Sections that address that program apply only if **[AGENCY NAME]** is separately approved and certified by HFS. They do not apply to a private-pay-only establishment.
front_matter.how_to_use:
# How to Use This Manual

**Organization.** The policies follow the order of the Part 295 subparts: General Provisions, Policies, Personnel, Resident Care and Services, Medications, Resident Rights, Records, Food Service, and Physical Plant. Each policy states the rule citation it implements, so staff and surveyors can trace the policy back to its source.

**Customize before use.** This manual is a template. Before it is used:

- Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]**, **[FACILITY NAME / ADDRESS]** and similar placeholder with facility-specific information.
- Fill in names, titles, phone numbers, schedules, fee amounts, staffing patterns and any program options (for example, whether the establishment offers a special dementia program or participates in Supportive Living).
- Delete or mark "not applicable" any policy that does not apply, such as Supportive Living provisions for a private-pay-only establishment or dementia-program provisions where no such program is offered. Record the reason.

**Adopt.** The governing body of **[AGENCY NAME]** must formally adopt the customized manual. Record the adoption date, the approving individuals or body, and the version number on the approval page.

**Keep it current.** Review the manual at least annually. Also review it whenever a law, rule, IDPH guidance or a change in operations affects a policy. Revise the affected policy, re-adopt it, record the revision date, and retain superseded versions. Watch in particular for:

- Public Act 104-0589 (HB 3392), which amends 210 ILCS 9/15, 35, 70, 135 and 150. Its Section 99 makes it effective on becoming law, but the ILGA page lists an effective date of 7/24/2026. Confirm the date and the current statutory text before relying on the amended provisions.
- Amendments to 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295. The text available when this manual was prepared was current through 48 Ill. Reg. 12026 (eff. 7/29/2024). Section 295.3000 shows a last amendment in 2004 and should be checked against the current JCAR text.

**Train staff.** All staff must be trained on this manual:

- Train at hire, on every revision, and on a recurring schedule.
- Document the training with dates, topics, trainer and attendee signatures.
- Keep training records in the employee file.

This supports the ongoing-training requirement for staff in 210 ILCS 9/35(a)(3) and the personnel and training provisions of 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000.

**Verify against the official text.** Policies paraphrase the rules and may not match the rule text word for word. Some Part 295 sections were available only as excerpts when this manual was drafted, so confirm each against the official text on ilga.gov before relying on it. If a policy conflicts with a statute or rule, the statute or rule controls.

**Appendix A.** Appendix A maps every official review item to the policy that satisfies it. Use it to prepare for licensure review, renewal and surveys, and to find gaps.
front_matter.regulatory_framework:
# Regulatory Framework

## Governing rules

This manual is built on the following authorities, cited by their exact cite text:

| Cite | Subject |
|---|---|
| **210 ILCS 9/15** | Assessment and service plan requirements |
| **210 ILCS 9/25** | License requirement |
| **210 ILCS 9/35** | Issuance of license; director qualifications and training; staffing; Alzheimer's/dementia special care disclosure |
| **210 ILCS 9/45** | Renewal of licenses |
| **210 ILCS 9/70** | Service requirements, including medication services |
| **210 ILCS 9/135** | Civil penalties |
| **210 ILCS 9/150** | Alzheimer and dementia programs; admission and retention limits |
| **Public Act 104-0589 (HB 3392)** | Amends 210 ILCS 9/15, 35, 70, 135 and 150 |
| **77 Ill. Adm. Code 295** | Assisted Living and Shared Housing Establishment Code (Subparts A–I) |
| **77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.500** | Application for License |
| **77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.600** | Initial license issuance |
| **77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000** | Residency Requirements |
| **77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2030** | Establishment Contracts |
| **77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000** | Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training |
| **225 ILCS 46** | Health Care Worker Background Check Act |
| **89 Ill. Adm. Code 146** | Supportive Living Program (HFS). Applies only if the facility is separately approved and certified by HFS. |

Part 295 is organized as follows: Subpart A General Provisions (295.1–295.1110); B Policies (295.2000–295.2080); C Personnel (295.3000–295.3050); D Resident Care and Services (295.4000–295.4060); E Medications (295.5000); F Resident Rights (295.6000–295.6030); G Resident and Establishment Records (295.7000–295.7010); H Food Service (295.8000); I Physical Plant and Environmental Requirements (295.9000–295.9040).

**Notes on currency.** Public Act 104-0589 amends the Act, and the ILGA page shows an effective date of 7/24/2026. Verify the status of the amended text. Section 295.3000 was last amended in 2004, so check it against the current JCAR text.

## Regulators and contacts

| Regulator | Role | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH), Division of Assisted Living** (Springfield) | State licensure and surveys of assisted living and shared housing establishments | https://dph.illinois.gov/topics-services/health-care-regulation/assisted-living.html |
| **IDPH Design and Construction Section** | Life Safety Code and physical plant surveys before licensure; review of construction drawings for new or major-alteration projects | https://dph.illinois.gov/topics-services/health-care-regulation/assisted-living.html |
| **Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS)** | Supportive Living Program (Medicaid 1915(c) waiver): provider approval, certification and per diem rates | Phone 1-844-528-8444; HFS.SLF@illinois.gov; https://hfs.illinois.gov/medicalclients/hcbs/slf.html |
| **HFS IMPACT** | Medicaid provider enrollment and eligibility management | https://hfs.illinois.gov/impact |
| **Illinois State Police** | Receives electronically collected fingerprints for Health Care Worker Background Check Act checks (within 10 working days) | https://www.ilga.gov/legislation/ilcs/ilcs3.asp?ActID=1303 |
| **Illinois Secretary of State** | LLC formation (Articles of Organization, Form LLC-5.5) and annual reports (Form LLC-50.1) | https://www.ilsos.gov/departments/business_services/home.html |

Phone numbers and email addresses for IDPH, HFS IMPACT, the Illinois State Police and the Secretary of State were not available when this manual was prepared. **[AGENCY NAME]** should add the current direct contacts for its assigned IDPH regional staff and licensing contacts here: **[INSERT CONTACT INFORMATION]**.

## Official policy checklist / review document

IDPH publishes **no** policy checklist, plan-of-operation form or provider-manual checklist for this license. License applications are submitted on Department-provided forms under 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.500. The Division of Assisted Living's page lists only a complaint form, involuntary-termination forms and a Life Safety Code inspection request.

The review document used for this manual is therefore the regulation itself: **Assisted Living and Shared Housing Establishment Code (77 Ill. Adm. Code 295), Subpart B – Policies (§§ 295.2000–295.2080), together with the policy-content sections of Subparts A and C.** It is issued by IDPH, Division of Assisted Living, and was current through 48 Ill. Reg. 12026, eff. 7/29/2024. Full text is at https://www.ilga.gov/agencies/JCAR/EntirePart?titlepart=07700295, with Cornell LII mirrors at https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/illinois/title-77/part-295/subpart-B and https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/illinois/Ill-Admin-Code-tit-77-SS-295.3000.

**Appendix A maps every official item to the policy that satisfies it.** The items are drawn from the Part 295 sections that require written policies and plans. At the application stage, the Department checks policy-type items such as the quality improvement program (§ 295.500(a)(8)), the service and contract documents (§ 295.500(a)(10) and (12)) and the disaster plan.

**Limits of the item list.** The list is incomplete. Sections 295.500, 295.2000 and 295.3000 were reviewed in full. Sections 295.2030, 295.2040, 295.2050 and 295.2060 were reviewed only as excerpts. Sections 295.2010, 295.2020, 295.2070 and 295.2080, 295.3010–295.3050, and Subparts D through I were not reviewed. Subpart D includes infection control at § 295.4045. Confirm all of these against the official text before relying on Appendix A.

## Customization, adoption, currency and training

- **Customize.** Replace all **[AGENCY NAME]** and other placeholders with facility-specific information before use.
- **Adopt.** The governing body must formally adopt the manual and record the date.
- **Keep current.** Review at least annually and whenever the law, rules or operations change, including any changes arising from Public Act 104-0589.
- **Train.** Train all staff on the manual at hire, on every revision and on a recurring schedule, and keep documentation of that training.

This manual is an operational tool and not legal advice. The statutes and rules listed above control.

citations.title: Assessment and service plan requirements
citations.requirement: Before admission, a comprehensive assessment of physical, cognitive and psychosocial condition must be completed by a physician, physician assistant or APRN. It must be repeated at least annually and on a significant change in condition, including a diagnosis of Alzheimer's or a related dementia. IDPH may set more frequent skin-integrity and nutrition assessments by rule. A written service plan is mutually agreed by provider, resident and representative and reviewed at least annually or when needs change. On request the resident or representative gets a copy of the latest assessment, any supplemental establishment assessment, and the service plan. Text as amended by P.A. 104-0589.

citations.title: Issuance of license
citations.requirement: A full-time director must be 21+ with a high school diploma or equivalent plus qualifying experience (35(a)(2)). Staff must be sufficient in number and skill for 24-hour scheduled and unscheduled needs and must take ongoing training (35(a)(3)). All employees subject to the Health Care Worker Background Check Act must meet it (35(a)(4)). Applicant must file the Alzheimer's/dementia special care disclosure document (35(a)(7)). As a condition of licensure the director must complete at least 20 hours of training every 2 years. Licenses last one year, state the physical location, issue and expiration dates, and are not transferable.

citations.title: Service requirements
citations.requirement: Defines medication reminders, supervision of self-administered medication and medication administration. Medication administration is by a licensed health care professional employed by the establishment. A certified medication aide may administer under RN supervision and delegation per Nurse Practice Act 50-75, except Schedule II controlled substances and any subcutaneous, intramuscular, intradermal or IV medication. Supervision of self-administered medication is under a licensed health care professional, or under RN delegation for a certified medication aide. IDPH sets procedures by rule. Services may be provided directly or by others arranged with resident consent.

citations.title: Civil penalties
citations.requirement: IDPH may assess a civil penalty of up to $5,000 per violation, with each day a separate violation. A penalty of up to $3,000 (also per day) may be assessed for caring for a resident who exceeds the care needs defined in the Act. Repeated technical infractions within a calendar year may become a Type 3 violation. IDPH may hold hearings on appeals.

citations.title: Alzheimer and dementia programs
citations.requirement: No admission or retention if the establishment cannot provide or secure appropriate care or lacks appropriately skilled staff. Residency is barred if the resident's condition has so deteriorated that residency is detrimental to the resident or others, or if the resident is dangerous and the danger cannot be eliminated. IDPH rule must identify a validated dementia-specific assessment standard with inter-rater reliability. That assessment is approved by the physician, or a PA/APRN with geriatric dementia experience. It is done before acceptance, annually, and on a change in condition. Annual and change-of-condition assessments must be signed by a physician. Establishments offering a special dementia program must disclose to IDPH and residents, ensure a designated representative, adopt wandering and evacuation safety policies, coordinate communications with family, provide cognitive stimulation and activities, staff appropriately, provide director and direct care staff dementia training, and have emergency procedures and staffing patterns. Pre-admission assessment tools must be validated for dementia-related cognitive impairment (150(g)).

citations.title: Amends 210 ILCS 9/15, 35, 70, 135 and 150
citations.requirement: Amends Sections 15, 35, 70, 135 and 150 of the Assisted Living and Shared Housing Act. Section 99 makes it effective on becoming law. The ILGA page shows Effective Date 7/24/2026.

citations.title: Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
citations.requirement: Requires sufficient qualified staff for 24-hour scheduled and unscheduled needs (a). Requires at least one direct care staff person on duty at all times with adult CPR training (including a skills demonstration) and current certification (b). Direct care staff must be 16+ at hire (c). Job descriptions must set minimum education and experience (d). Employee files must hold the items in (e) and (f). Records are kept for employment plus at least 12 months (g). Staffing must cover the services listed in (h). Personnel schedules must meet (i). Awake staff are required for residents who cannot self-move to safety (j). Shared housing needs at least one staff member on site at all times (k). Assisted living needs at least one staff member awake, on duty and on site 24 hours (l). Nurse Aide Registry check before hire, with no hiring of anyone with a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation (m). Licensed-staff license verification (n). Cornell shows this section's history as last amended in 2004, so check it against the current JCAR text.

citations.title: Establishment Contracts
citations.requirement: The contract must be titled 'assisted living establishment contract' or 'shared housing establishment contract' and printed in at least 12-point type. It must contain the 20 elements in (a), including: license status; base rate and services; extra services and fee schedule; complaint process with notice of the Department on Aging Senior Helpline and the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program; the Medicaid statement; admission and termination criteria; a risk management statement; and the Section 95 rights list. It must also include a statement from IDPH on the annual on-site review process. Under (b) it must include fee/deposit/refund terms, 30 days' written notice of fee changes (not required where service needs change per the service plan), and an emergency/relative notification policy. A copy goes to the resident or representative, and the signed contract stays on premises. Contracts may auto-renew yearly, and changes must be written and signed by both parties.

citations.title: License requirement
citations.requirement: No person may establish, operate, maintain or offer an assisted living or shared housing establishment without a license (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Renewal of licenses
citations.requirement: Renewal application is filed 120-150 days before expiration. IDPH 'may' grant a 2-year renewal at the licensee's request only if, in the preceding 24 months, there was no Type 1 or Type 2 violation, no inspection with 10 or more Type 3 violations, and no admission or retention in violation of Section 75 (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Application for License
citations.requirement: Nonrefundable fee of $2,000 + $20 per unit for assisted living, $1,000 for shared housing. The application states standard vs. floating licensure, includes liability insurance documentation, and shows financial capacity (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Initial license issuance
citations.requirement: IDPH issues a regular license within 120 days of a complete application. Approval needs fees paid, substantial compliance, and Background Check Act compliance for covered employees (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Residency Requirements
citations.requirement: An establishment may not accept or retain a resident when it lacks staff appropriate in numbers and skill, or cannot provide or secure the required services (per fact-checked research). Read the full text for the complete list of conditions.

citations.title: Health Care Worker Background Check Act
citations.requirement: Covers employees with or who may have resident contact. Fingerprints are collected electronically and sent to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Supportive Living Program
citations.requirement: HFS rules for Medicaid Supportive Living. Applies only if the facility is separately approved and certified by HFS. It does not apply to an IDPH-licensed establishment that is private pay only.

citations.title: Assisted Living and Shared Housing Establishment Code
citations.requirement: Subparts, as confirmed on the LII table of contents: A General Provisions (295.1-295.1110); B Policies (295.2000-295.2080); C Personnel (295.3000-295.3050); D Resident Care and Services (295.4000-295.4060); E Medications (295.5000); F Resident Rights (295.6000-295.6030); G Resident and Establishment Records (295.7000-295.7010); H Food Service (295.8000); I Physical Plant and Environmental Requirements (295.9000-295.9040). The LII notes show amendments through 7/29/2024.

policies.category: Subpart A – General Provisions: § 295.500 Application for License
policies.title: IDPH License Application, Standard vs. Floating Licensure, Renewal and Posting
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment – governing body, Administrator/Manager, business office
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] holds a valid Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH) license before it operates, that the license application states the type of licensure requested, and that the license is renewed on time and kept current and posted.
policies.policy: No person may establish, operate, maintain or offer an assisted living or shared housing establishment in Illinois without an IDPH license (210 ILCS 9/25). [AGENCY NAME] will not admit a resident, begin services or let any contract take effect until IDPH has issued the license. This policy meets 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.500(b): every application states whether [AGENCY NAME] requests standard licensure or floating licensure. A floating-license application must comply with Section 32 of the Act and Section 295.1110. The nonrefundable application fee is $2,000 plus $20 per licensed unit for assisted living, or $1,000 for shared housing, and is paid with the application. IDPH issues a regular license within 120 days of a complete application, provided fees are paid, the establishment is in substantial compliance and covered employees meet the Health Care Worker Background Check Act. A license lasts one year, states the physical location and the issue and expiration dates, and is not transferable. The renewal application is filed 120–150 days before expiration. A 2-year renewal is available only at our request, only if IDPH chooses to grant it, and only if in the preceding 24 months there was no Type 1 or Type 2 violation, no inspection with 10 or more Type 3 violations, and no admission or retention in violation of Section 75. Public Act 104-0589 (HB 3392), which amends Sections 15, 35, 70, 135 and 150 of the Act, is monitored and applied from its confirmed effective date.

definitions.definition: The ordinary IDPH establishment license requested in the application for the physical location stated on the license.
A license requested in an application that must comply with Section 32 of the Act and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.1110.
IDPH's classifications of violations found at inspection. They determine eligibility for a 2-year renewal and exposure to civil penalties.
A resident unit counted by IDPH for the per-unit portion of the assisted living application fee.
The period from 150 days to 120 days before the license expiration date, during which the renewal application must be filed.

procedures: Before applying, the governing body confirms in writing whether [AGENCY NAME] will operate as an assisted living establishment or a shared housing establishment and states the number of units. The Administrator files this in the License Application File.

The governing body decides whether to request standard or floating licensure and records the decision in its minutes. The Administrator marks the request on the IDPH application: [STANDARD OR FLOATING – SELECT ONE].

If floating licensure is requested, the Administrator reviews Section 32 of the Act and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.1110 line by line, prepares a checklist of what each requires, and attaches every required item to the application.

The Administrator calculates the fee: $2,000 plus $20 per licensed unit for assisted living (for example, 40 units = $2,800), or $1,000 for shared housing. The fee is paid with the application and is nonrefundable. The calculation sheet and proof of payment go in the License Application File.

The Administrator assembles the supporting documents: liability insurance documentation, evidence of financial capacity, the standard contract (APP-02), the director's qualifications (PER-05), proof that covered employees meet the Background Check Act (PER-04), and, if a special Alzheimer's/dementia program is offered, the disclosure document required by 210 ILCS 9/35(a)(7) (CARE-04).

The Administrator checks the full packet against the IDPH application form and this policy's checklist. An authorized signer designated by the governing body ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME] or [OWNER NAME]) signs the application. A complete copy is kept.
The Administrator submits the application to the IDPH Division of Assisted Living and records the date, method and any tracking number in the License Application Log.

The Administrator calendars day 120 from the date IDPH received a complete application. The Administrator answers every IDPH request for information within the deadline IDPH sets. If no license has been issued by day 120, the Administrator contacts IDPH in writing and records the contact.

For new construction or major alteration, the Administrator coordinates drawings and Life Safety Code review with the IDPH Design and Construction Section under PP-01 and PP-03 and keeps approvals in the License Application File.

On receiving the license, the Administrator verifies the establishment name, physical address [ADDRESS], issue and expiration dates, and one-year term. Any error is reported to IDPH in writing within 5 business days.

The Administrator posts the license in a conspicuous place that residents and visitors can see, at [POSTING LOCATION], and keeps a copy in the License File. The original is never altered or moved to another location or entity.

The Administrator sets calendar reminders at 210, 180, 150 and 120 days before expiration. The internal target for filing renewal is 140 days before expiration, which is inside the 120–150 day window.

Before each renewal, the Administrator reviews the preceding 24 months of IDPH survey results and the admission and retention records. The review records whether there was any Type 1 or Type 2 violation, any inspection with 10 or more Type 3 violations, or any Section 75 admission or retention violation.

If all three 2-year-renewal conditions are met, the Administrator may ask the governing body to approve a written request for a 2-year renewal. The Administrator understands that IDPH 'may' grant it and does not treat it as automatic. If any condition is not met, the Administrator files for the one-year renewal.

The Administrator files the renewal application and fee within the renewal window. The Administrator also verifies that the full-time director has the age, education and experience required under 210 ILCS 9/35(a)(2) and is on track for the 20 hours of director training every 2 years (PER-05).

If the establishment is sold, relocated or restructured, the Administrator informs IDPH before the change takes effect and does not assume the license transfers, because licenses are not transferable. The governing body does not operate under another entity's license.

If a license has expired or lapsed, or a renewal was not filed on time, the Administrator notifies the governing body the same day, contacts IDPH, and obtains legal advice about continued operation before any new admission.

The Administrator checks the ILGA record for Public Act 104-0589 (HB 3392) and confirms its effective date. The ILGA page shows an effective date of 7/24/2026. The Administrator updates affected policies (director training, civil penalties, admission assessment, dementia programs) before that date and documents the review.
The Administrator reviews this policy at least annually with the governing body (GOV-01).

policies.title: Service Delivery Contract Verification and Standard Contract Copy for IDPH
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment – Administrator/Manager, admissions and business office
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident or resident's representative signs a contract that meets 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2030, and that IDPH receives verification of this practice and a copy of the standard contract with the license application.
policies.policy: This policy meets 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.500(a)(5) (verification that the establishment has entered or will enter into a service delivery contract under Section 295.2030 with each resident or resident's representative) and 295.500(a)(12) (a copy of the standard contract offered to residents). [AGENCY NAME] will not admit a resident until the resident or the resident's representative has signed a contract meeting Section 295.2030. The application includes a signed statement that [AGENCY NAME] has entered or will enter into such a contract with each resident or representative. The standard contract offered to residents is filed with the application. The signed contract is kept on the premises. A copy goes to the resident or representative. The Administrator re-files the standard contract with IDPH whenever IDPH rules change in a way that affects contract content.

definitions.definition: The written agreement titled 'assisted living establishment contract' or 'shared housing establishment contract' between the establishment and each resident or the resident's representative.
The unsigned contract form that [AGENCY NAME] offers to every prospective resident, filed with IDPH.
The person authorized to sign the contract and act for the resident (RTS-03).
The statement in the license application, signed by the authorized signer, that contracts have been or will be entered into with each resident as Section 295.2030 requires.

procedures: The Administrator drafts the standard contract using the content rules in CON-01 and CON-02, so that it carries the title 'assisted living establishment contract' or 'shared housing establishment contract' and is printed in at least 12-point type.

The Administrator checks the draft against each of the 20 elements in 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2030(a). These include license status, base rate and services, extra services and fee schedule, the complaint process with notice of the Department on Aging Senior Helpline and the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program, the Medicaid statement, admission and termination criteria, a risk management statement, and the Section 95 rights list.

The Administrator checks the draft against Section 295.2030(b) and confirms it contains fee, deposit and refund terms, 30 days' written notice of fee changes (not required where charges change because the service plan changed), and the emergency and relative notification policy.
The Administrator confirms the contract includes the IDPH statement on the annual on-site review process.
The governing body or legal counsel reviews the standard contract before it is filed or used. The reviewer's name and date are recorded on the Contract Review Sheet.

The Administrator files a copy of the standard contract with the IDPH license application as the item required by 295.500(a)(12). The Administrator marks the exhibit number on the application checklist.
The authorized signer completes the verification statement required by 295.500(a)(5) in the application. A copy is kept in the License Application File.
At admission, the admissions staff member gives the prospective resident or representative the standard contract in advance. Staff explain it and offer language assistance (RTS-06) before signature.

The resident or representative and an authorized agent of [AGENCY NAME] sign and date the contract. No move-in occurs until both signatures are on the contract and the Administrator has checked the admission eligibility decision (RES-01 to RES-03).
The Administrator gives a complete copy of the signed contract to the resident or representative and records the date and the recipient's name on the Contract Delivery Log.
The original signed contract is kept on the premises in the resident's record or the locked contract file (REC-01). It is available to IDPH during surveys.
Contracts may renew automatically each year. Any change to a signed contract must be written and signed by both parties. Staff do not make oral changes.

The Administrator reviews the standard contract at least annually and whenever IDPH rules change. If the standard contract is revised, the Administrator re-files the updated copy with IDPH, notes the filing date, and offers current residents any change by written amendment signed by both parties.
The Administrator checks a sample of resident files each quarter to confirm every resident has a signed, complete contract on the premises. Findings go to the Quality Improvement committee (QI-01).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the standard contract, files it with IDPH, re-files after rule changes, and ensures no resident moves in without a signed contract.
Signs the application verification statement and resident contracts.
Provide the contract in advance, explain it, obtain signatures, deliver copies and log delivery.
Reviews the standard contract for compliance with Section 295.2030.
Reviews quarterly contract audit results.

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2000 Residency Requirements
policies.title: Admission Eligibility: Who May and May Not Be Accepted (Functional and Behavioral Criteria)
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment – Administrator/Manager, admissions staff, assessing clinician, direct care staff
policies.purpose: To set clear, consistent criteria for deciding who [AGENCY NAME] may accept and retain, based on the individual's functional and behavioral needs and our actual staffing, services and building.
policies.policy: This policy meets 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000(a), (b) and (c)(1) through (c)(5). (a) No individual is accepted for residency or allowed to remain if [AGENCY NAME] cannot provide or secure appropriate services, if the individual needs a level or type of service we are not licensed for or do not provide, or if we lack staff appropriate in numbers and skill (also Act Sec. 75(a) and 210 ILCS 9/150). (b) Only adults are accepted. (c)(1) We do not accept a person who poses a serious threat to self or others. (c)(2) We do not accept a person who cannot communicate needs in any manner, unless a resident representative who lives in the establishment and had a prior relationship with the person has been appointed to direct services. (c)(3) We do not accept a person who requires total assistance with 2 or more activities of daily living (ADLs). (c)(4) We do not accept a person who requires more than one paid caregiver at any given time for an ADL. (c)(5) We do not accept a person who requires more than minimal assistance to move to a safe area in an emergency. 'Minimal assistance' means the resident can respond, with or without assistance, to protect themselves given our staffing and the construction of the building. Under 210 ILCS 9/150, residency is also barred if the resident's condition has so deteriorated that residency is detrimental to the resident or others, or if the resident is dangerous and the danger cannot be eliminated. These criteria apply at admission and continue to apply throughout residency. Acceptance is decided on the documented pre-admission assessment (CARE-01), not on marketing or occupancy goals.

definitions.definition: Basic self-care tasks such as eating, bathing, dressing, toileting, transferring and mobility, as assessed in the comprehensive assessment.
The resident cannot perform any meaningful part of the ADL and staff must do the whole task.
The resident can respond, with or without assistance, to protect themselves and reach a safe area, given our staffing levels and building construction.
A documented, current risk of serious harm to the person or others, based on behavior, history and current clinical information.

definitions.term: Resident representative residing in the establishment
definitions.definition: A person who lives in the establishment, had a prior relationship with the individual, and is appointed to direct services for an individual who cannot communicate needs.

procedures: Admissions staff use the Admission Eligibility Checklist for every inquiry that reaches the application stage. The checklist lists each criterion in 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000(a), (b) and (c)(1) through (c)(5).
Admissions staff confirm the applicant is an adult by verifying a government-issued ID or other proof of age. A person under 18 is not accepted.

The Administrator arranges the pre-admission comprehensive assessment under CARE-01. The assessment is completed by a qualified professional and uses the dementia-validated tool where required under 210 ILCS 9/150. For an applicant with cognitive impairment, the physician, or a PA/APRN with geriatric dementia experience, approves the assessment before acceptance.

Admissions staff gather records from the applicant, family, hospital or physician: medical history, medication list, behavior history, communication ability, mobility and transfer needs. They attach these to the checklist.

The assessing professional records for each ADL whether the person is independent, needs limited help, needs extensive help, or needs total assistance. The assessment records how many staff are needed at once for each ADL.

The Administrator screens for (c)(1) by reviewing behavior history, any violence, self-harm or threats, and clinician input. If a serious threat to self or others is documented, the person is not accepted. The Administrator records the reasons.

The Administrator screens for (c)(2) by observing and documenting how the person communicates needs by speech, writing, gesture or device. If the person cannot communicate needs in any manner, the Administrator confirms whether a resident representative who lives in the establishment and had a prior relationship has been appointed. If not, the person is not accepted.

The Administrator applies (c)(3): if the person needs total assistance with 2 or more ADLs, the person is not accepted. The Administrator applies (c)(4): if any ADL requires more than one paid caregiver at the same time, the person is not accepted.

The Administrator applies (c)(5) by comparing the person's ability to respond in an emergency with the current evacuation capability of the building and the staffing on each shift. The comparison uses the most recent drill evaluations (DIS-03, PP-03). If the person needs more than minimal assistance to reach a safe area, the person is not accepted.

The Administrator applies (a) by confirming in writing that [AGENCY NAME] can provide or secure each service in the service plan, holds the license needed for it, and has staff sufficient in numbers and skill on every shift, including nights (PER-01, PER-02). If any answer is no, the person is not accepted.
Before final acceptance the Administrator also reviews the exclusions in RES-02 and the exceptions in RES-03 and records the decision on the checklist. The Administrator signs and dates the decision.

If the person is not accepted, the Administrator tells the applicant or representative in writing the same day the decision is made, states the reason, and offers help finding other options. The notice is not discriminatory (RTS-06). Staff keep a copy in the inquiry file.
If accepted, admissions staff proceed to the contract (CON-01, APP-02) and the service plan (CARE-01). The Administrator confirms the contract includes the admission criteria.

After admission, staff re-check these criteria at each reassessment and on every change of condition (CARE-01, CARE-05). If a resident no longer meets the criteria, the Administrator starts the review under TERM-01 within one business day.

The Administrator audits all admissions every quarter for compliance with this policy and reports the results to the Quality Improvement committee (QI-01). Any admission found to violate 295.2000 is reported to the governing body immediately.

responsibilities.duty: Makes and signs every acceptance or denial decision and confirms staffing and service capability.
Complete the checklist, collect records and notify applicants of decisions.

responsibilities.role: Assessing professional (physician, PA/APRN or other qualified person as required)
responsibilities.duty: Completes the pre-admission assessment and records ADL, communication and emergency-response findings.
Report changes in function or behavior that could affect continued eligibility.
Receives quarterly audit results and ensures resources match the residents accepted.

documentation: Admission Eligibility Checklist signed by the Administrator
Pre-admission comprehensive assessment and dementia-validated tool results, where required
Proof of age and records received from the applicant
Denial notices and reasons
Staffing and service capability confirmation
Quarterly admission audit reports

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2000 Residency Requirements
policies.title: Admission Exclusions: Severe Mental Illness and Clinical Treatment Conditions
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment – Administrator/Manager, admissions staff, assessing clinician, nursing consultant
policies.purpose: To state which mental health conditions and clinical treatments exclude a person from admission or continued residency, and to explain how [AGENCY NAME] applies those exclusions and respects each resident's right to choose a licensed provider.
policies.policy: This policy meets 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000(c)(6) through (c)(13) and 295.2000(h). (c)(6) We do not accept a person with a severe mental illness, meaning a DSM-5-TR major mental disorder with substantial disability expected to last at least one year. Alzheimer's disease and other dementias based on organic or physical disorders are excluded from this definition. A diagnosis of depression alone does not bar residency unless the resident is substantially disabled in the areas listed in the rule. (c)(7) We do not accept a person who requires intravenous therapy or feedings unless self-administered or administered by a qualified, licensed health care professional. (c)(8) Same for gastrostomy feedings. (c)(9) Same for insertion, sterile irrigation and replacement of a catheter; routine maintenance of urinary catheters is allowed. (c)(10) Same for sterile wound care. (c)(11) Same for a diabetic requiring routine insulin injections. (c)(12) We do not accept a person who requires treatment of stage 3 or stage 4 decubitus ulcers or exfoliative dermatitis. (c)(13) We do not accept a person who requires 5 or more skilled nursing visits per week, for conditions other than those in (c)(12), for 3 consecutive weeks or more, unless the course of treatment is expected to extend beyond 3 weeks for rehabilitative purposes and a physician certifies it as temporary. (h) For (c)(7) through (c)(10), the licensed health care professional may not be employed by the owner or operator, its parent entity, or any entity with common ownership, including affiliates, and nothing limits a resident's right to choose their health care provider. Staff of [AGENCY NAME] do not perform the treatments in (c)(7) through (c)(11) for a resident. A person with dementia is evaluated under RES-01, CARE-04 and 210 ILCS 9/150, not excluded by (c)(6) on the basis of dementia alone.

definitions.definition: A DSM-5-TR major mental disorder with substantial disability expected to last at least one year, as defined in 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000. Alzheimer's disease and other organic dementias are excluded from the definition.
The resident personally performs the treatment or injection without hands-on performance by staff.
A professional licensed in Illinois to perform the treatment (for example, a registered nurse), who is not employed by or affiliated with the owner or operator as described in 295.2000(h).
Ordinary care of an indwelling urinary catheter that is allowed. It does not include insertion, sterile irrigation or replacement.
A visit by a licensed nurse to provide skilled care, counted per week for the 5-visit/3-week test.

procedures: Admissions staff add the (c)(6) through (c)(13) screening questions to the Admission Eligibility Checklist. Staff review each applicant's diagnoses, treatment orders and recent hospital or home health records against each exclusion.

For (c)(6), the Administrator obtains the applicant's psychiatric and primary care records and asks the assessing professional whether the person has a DSM-5-TR major mental disorder with substantial disability expected to last at least one year. Staff do not diagnose. The Administrator documents the professional's response and the reasoning.
If the applicant has dementia, the Administrator confirms the dementia is organic and not a (c)(6) exclusion, then continues review under RES-01 and CARE-04.

If the applicant has a diagnosis of depression alone, the Administrator confirms with the assessing professional that the person is not substantially disabled in the areas the rule lists. The Administrator records this.

For (c)(7) through (c)(11), the Administrator reviews the medication and treatment orders for IV therapy or feedings, gastrostomy feedings, catheter insertion, sterile irrigation or replacement, sterile wound care and routine insulin injections.

If a treatment in (c)(7) through (c)(11) is needed, the Administrator asks whether the resident will self-administer it. The assessing professional documents the resident's ability and willingness to do so, and the resident's actual performance is observed and recorded. If the resident cannot self-administer, the person may be accepted only if a qualified licensed health care professional will administer the treatment.

For (c)(7) through (c)(10), the Administrator confirms the licensed professional is not employed by the owner or operator, its parent entity, or any entity with common ownership, including affiliates. The Administrator checks the provider's name against the ownership and affiliate list kept in the Governing Body file. A provider who fails this check is not used.

Admissions staff tell the resident or representative in writing that the resident may choose their own licensed health care provider and that [AGENCY NAME] will not steer the resident to an affiliated provider. The resident signs an acknowledgment, and a copy goes in the admission file.

Staff of [AGENCY NAME] do not perform any treatment listed in (c)(7) through (c)(11) for a resident, except as a visiting licensed professional from an allowed provider. Staff may remind, set up the environment, and observe a resident who self-administers. They follow MED-01 for medication handling.
For (c)(9), staff may perform routine maintenance of a urinary catheter only within their training and job description, with documentation in the service plan.

For (c)(12), the Administrator screens skin records and wound descriptions. A person needing treatment of a stage 3 or stage 4 decubitus ulcer or exfoliative dermatitis is not accepted. A current resident who develops one is referred for review under TERM-01 the same day the condition is identified (see CARE-06).

For (c)(13), the Administrator asks the referral source and home health agency how many skilled nursing visits per week are ordered and for how long. If 5 or more visits per week are needed for 3 consecutive weeks or more for conditions other than those in (c)(12), the person is not accepted.

If a rehabilitative course extends beyond 3 weeks, the Administrator obtains a written physician certification that the course is temporary and records its expected end date. The Administrator re-checks on that date.

For current residents, the nurse consultant or assessing professional re-screens against these exclusions at every reassessment and change of condition (CARE-01, CARE-05). Any resident who now meets an exclusion is referred to the Administrator the same day for review under TERM-01.

If a person is denied under this policy, the Administrator gives the applicant or representative a written explanation and referral suggestions. The Administrator keeps the decision record for audit by IDPH.
The Administrator audits a sample of admissions and reassessments each quarter for compliance and reports the results to the Quality Improvement committee (QI-01).

responsibilities.duty: Makes the final decision on each exclusion, checks provider independence and records the resident's provider choice.
Evaluates mental health status, treatment needs, self-administration ability, skin condition and skilled nursing visit frequency.
Screen records, explain the provider-choice right and keep checklists.
Report new treatments, wounds, catheter issues or behavior changes immediately and never perform excluded treatments.
Maintains the list of owners, parent entities and affiliates used for the 295.2000(h) check.

documentation: Admission Eligibility Checklist with (c)(6)–(c)(13) screening completed
Assessing professional's documentation on severe mental illness
Self-administration assessments and observation notes
Provider independence check against the ownership and affiliate list
Resident acknowledgment of the right to choose a health care provider
Physician certification that a rehabilitative course is temporary, if applicable
Denial letters and quarterly audit reports

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2000 Residency Requirements
policies.title: Residency Exceptions (Hospice, Physical Disability) and Pre-Admission Vaccine Advice
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment – Administrator/Manager, admissions staff, nurse consultant, direct care staff
policies.purpose: To define when [AGENCY NAME] may keep a terminally ill resident under hospice, when the physical disability exception applies, and how we give the required pre-admission vaccine advice.
policies.policy: This policy meets 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000(f), (g) and (i). (f) Subsection (d) (mandatory termination for conditions in (c)) does not apply to terminally ill residents who receive or would qualify for hospice care coordinated by a licensed hospice program or by a licensed health care professional employed by a licensed home health agency, when [AGENCY NAME] and all parties agree to continued residency. (g) Subsections (c)(3), (c)(4), (c)(5) and (c)(9) do not apply to individuals who are quadriplegic or paraplegic, or who have neuro-muscular diseases or other chronic conditions, if the individual can communicate needs, does not need assistance with complex medical problems, and [AGENCY NAME] can accommodate the individual's needs. (i) Before admission, if [AGENCY NAME] does not provide medication administration as an optional service, we advise each prospective resident to consult a physician about pneumococcal pneumonia and/or influenza vaccination (Act Sec. 76). Our medication administration status is: [OFFERS / DOES NOT OFFER – SELECT ONE]. The advice is documented in the admission file. An exception is never a reason to exceed our staffing or skill, and the requirements of RES-01, 210 ILCS 9/150 and 295.2000(a) continue to apply.

definitions.definition: Comfort-focused care for a terminally ill person, coordinated by a licensed hospice program or by a licensed health care professional employed by a licensed home health agency.
A resident whose physician has determined that the resident has a terminal illness and who receives, or would qualify for, hospice care.
The 295.2000(g) exception that lifts (c)(3), (c)(4), (c)(5) and (c)(9) for qualifying residents, as described in this policy.
Medical needs beyond what staff may provide or secure under this establishment's license, services and staffing, as determined by the assessing professional.
A written statement given before admission advising the prospective resident to consult a physician about pneumococcal pneumonia and/or influenza vaccination.

procedures: When a resident is terminally ill, or a prospective resident is terminally ill, the Administrator requests a written physician statement of the terminal diagnosis and confirms the person receives hospice or would qualify for it.

The Administrator confirms the hospice care will be coordinated by a licensed hospice program or by a licensed health care professional employed by a licensed home health agency. The Administrator obtains the provider's name, license information and contact number and files them (CARE-07).

The Administrator holds a care conference with the resident or representative, the hospice or home health provider, the physician if available, and [AGENCY NAME] clinical staff. The group decides whether continued residency is appropriate and agrees on who provides which services.

All parties must agree to continued residency. The agreement is written, signed and dated by the resident or representative, the hospice or home health provider and the Administrator. If any party does not agree, residency is reviewed under TERM-01.

The service plan is updated to include the hospice plan of care, staff roles and emergency steps (CARE-01, CARE-07). Staffing is verified as sufficient in numbers and skill for the added needs (PER-01).

The Administrator reviews the hospice exception with the care team at least every 30 days and at each change of condition, and documents whether the agreement still holds. If staffing or skill is no longer sufficient, the Administrator informs the resident or representative and begins review under TERM-01.

For physical disability, the Administrator receives the diagnosis (for example, quadriplegia, paraplegia, neuro-muscular disease or other chronic condition) and requests a written assessment from the qualified professional (CARE-01).

The assessing professional documents that the individual can communicate needs, does not need assistance with complex medical problems, and that [AGENCY NAME] can accommodate the individual's needs. This includes transfers, equipment, ADL help and the person's ability to evacuate with the staff and building we have.

The Administrator reviews the building accessibility, evacuation plan and staffing for the person (PP-01, PP-03, DIS-03). The review must show that the specific needs can be met. If so, the Administrator records the use of the 295.2000(g) exception on the Admission Eligibility Checklist and signs it.

The exception applies only to (c)(3), (c)(4), (c)(5) and (c)(9). All other criteria in RES-01 and RES-02 still apply. The Administrator re-reviews the exception at each reassessment and change of condition.

Before admission, admissions staff confirm whether [AGENCY NAME] provides medication administration as an optional service. If we do not, staff give each prospective resident a written Vaccine Advice Notice stating that the person should consult a physician about pneumococcal pneumonia and/or influenza vaccination.
Staff do not give medical advice or recommend a specific vaccination themselves. The notice directs the person to a physician. Staff may help the person arrange an appointment if asked.

The prospective resident or representative signs and dates the notice. If the person declines to sign, the staff member notes this on the form and signs it. The notice is placed in the admission file before move-in.
The Administrator audits new admission files monthly to confirm the vaccine advice is present when required and reports gaps to the Quality Improvement committee (QI-01).

responsibilities.duty: Decides whether an exception applies, obtains signed agreements and ensures staffing and building capability before relying on any exception.
Documents the hospice or disability assessment and re-reviews at each change of condition.
Coordinates and delivers hospice care and participates in the written agreement.
Deliver the Vaccine Advice Notice, collect signatures and file it before move-in.
Carry out the updated service plan and report changes to the Administrator or nurse consultant.

documentation: Physician statement of terminal diagnosis and hospice or home health provider information
Written agreement among the resident or representative, hospice provider and Administrator
Hospice care plan integrated into the service plan
Physical disability assessment and evacuation review
Admission Eligibility Checklist noting the exception used
Signed Vaccine Advice Notice in the admission file
Monthly audit of vaccine advice and exception reviews

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2010 Termination of Residency
policies.title: Termination of Residency, Discharge and Relocation Notice
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment – governing body, Administrator/Manager, nurse consultant, social services, direct care staff
policies.purpose: To make sure residency is ended only when 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000 and 295.2010 require or permit it, that residents get proper written notice, and that every resident is helped to relocate safely.
policies.policy: This policy meets 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000(d) and 295.2000(e). (d) A resident who has a condition listed in 295.2000(c) has residency terminated in accordance with Section 295.2010, unless the hospice exception in 295.2000(f) applies (RES-03). (e) Residency is terminated in accordance with Section 295.2010 when the services available in [AGENCY NAME] are no longer adequate to meet the resident's needs. This does not limit IDPH's authority to require termination of residency. [AGENCY NAME] follows the grounds, notice periods, notice content and procedures in 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2010 exactly as currently in effect. The Administrator keeps the current text of that Section on file and uses it to complete the Termination Notice Checklist. No notice is issued until the Administrator has checked it against that text. Staff never force a resident out without a written notice, and they never lock out, remove belongings, or withhold services as a way to end residency. Keeping a resident whose needs exceed what the Act allows can result in a civil penalty of up to $3,000 per day under 210 ILCS 9/135, so we act promptly once a termination ground is identified. The admission and termination criteria are also stated in the resident contract (CON-01). Closure of the whole establishment is handled under CLO-01.

definitions.definition: The ending of a resident's right to live in [AGENCY NAME], carried out under 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2010.
The internal checklist built from the current text of 295.2010. It lists each ground, notice period, content item and delivery requirement and is signed by the Administrator.
The point at which the services available in the establishment cannot meet the resident's assessed needs, even with reasonable adjustments to the service plan.
The planned and safe transfer of a resident to another living setting or level of care.
A condition or need listed in 295.2000(c) that excludes a person from admission and requires termination under 295.2000(d).

procedures: Before this policy is adopted, and at each annual policy review, the Administrator obtains the current official text of 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2010, confirms the grounds, notice periods and required notice content, and files a dated copy with the Termination Notice Checklist (GOV-01).
Any staff member who observes that a resident may have a condition in 295.2000(c), or that the resident's needs are no longer met, reports it to the nurse consultant or Administrator the same day.

The nurse consultant or assessing professional completes a reassessment within a time set by the Administrator, no later than 3 business days after the report. The reassessment compares the resident's needs with RES-01 and RES-02 criteria and with our services and staffing (CARE-01).

The Administrator holds a meeting with the resident, representative, family and physician as appropriate. The group reviews whether changes to the service plan, extra services, a negotiated risk agreement (NRA-01) or hospice (RES-03, CARE-07) could keep residency appropriate and lawful.
If the resident is terminally ill and meets the hospice exception, the Administrator follows RES-03. If any party withdraws agreement, the Administrator continues with the steps below.

If a listed condition or inadequate services is confirmed, the Administrator informs the resident or representative promptly, in plain language and in the resident's preferred language (RTS-06), that termination of residency will follow under 295.2010.

The Administrator completes the Termination Notice Checklist from the current text of 295.2010 and enters each required notice period, content item, delivery method and recipient. A second person, [DESIGNEE NAME], verifies it before the notice is issued.

The Administrator prepares the written notice with every item the checklist requires. The notice states the specific reason, the date, how to challenge the decision, and how to reach the Long-Term Care Ombudsman and the Department on Aging Senior Helpline (RTS-04).

The Administrator delivers the notice to the resident and representative by the method and within the period required by 295.2010, and records the date, method and recipient on the Notice Delivery Log.

Social services staff start relocation planning at the time of notice. They identify appropriate settings, such as a nursing facility or another residence that can meet the resident's needs, and help with tours, transfers and paperwork.
The nurse consultant coordinates with the resident's physician and the receiving provider. Records, medication lists and the service plan go with the resident as permitted by RTS-05.

If a resident's immediate safety is at risk, staff act first to protect the resident, including calling 911 and following CARE-05. The Administrator then follows 295.2010 for any termination that results.

On the move-out date, staff review the resident's personal property and funds with the resident or representative, return all items, and complete a final accounting and any refund due (CON-02, CON-03).
The Administrator keeps all termination documents in the resident's record (REC-01) and reports to IDPH any serious incident or required notice as set out in INC-01 and REC-02.
If IDPH requires termination of a resident's residency, the Administrator informs the resident or representative, follows 295.2010 and works with IDPH on the timeline.

The Quality Improvement committee reviews every termination quarterly for timeliness, notice accuracy and whether earlier intervention was possible (QI-01). The Administrator reports any admission or retention that exceeded 295.2000 to the governing body at once.

responsibilities.duty: Decides on termination, completes the checklist, issues the notice, and oversees relocation and final accounting.
Reassesses the resident, identifies listed conditions and coordinates with physicians and receiving providers.
Help the resident and family find and move to an appropriate setting.
Report changes in condition promptly and continue care until the resident leaves.
Receives reports on terminations and ensures the Administrator has the resources and current rule text to comply.

documentation: Current copy of 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2010 with date retrieved
Reassessment showing a listed condition or inadequate services
Care conference notes and alternatives considered
Completed and verified Termination Notice Checklist
Copy of the written notice and Notice Delivery Log
Relocation plan, receiving provider records and transfer documents
Final accounting, property return receipt and refund record
Quarterly termination review for Quality Improvement

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2020 Notice of Closure
policies.title: Facility Closure Notice and Resident Relocation
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment; governing body, administrator, nursing/care staff, business office
policies.purpose: To make sure that, if [AGENCY NAME] ever closes, the Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH), residents, residents' representatives and the Long-Term Care Ombudsman receive timely written notice. Each resident must be relocated safely, with continuity of care, an accounting of funds and deposits, and preserved records.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not close, in whole or in part, without first giving the notice required by the Notice of Closure section of Subpart B (Policies) of 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295 (Part 295, cited here as C16). The notice deadlines to IDPH and to residents are those stated in the current rule text. The administrator will read that text at the time a closure is considered and will record the exact deadlines, with the date they were verified, in the Closure Plan. The deadlines are not restated here so that this policy cannot become out of date. The administrator leads relocation planning and notifies residents, representatives, the Ombudsman and IDPH. No resident will be relocated without an individualized plan. All resident funds and deposits will be accounted for and refunded under the contract refund policy (CON-02 and CON-03). Resident records will remain available after closure under the Records policy (REC-01).

definitions.definition: The permanent cessation of operation of the establishment, or of the licensed unit or program, that requires residents to relocate.
The written plan prepared by the administrator that lists the notice deadlines, the notices sent, each resident's relocation plan, the funds reconciliation, and the records custodian.
The person identified in the resident's contract or records as authorized to act for the resident (see RTS-03).
The Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program, whose contact information is given to residents in the contract (CON-01) and the grievance policy (RTS-04).

procedures: Governing body decision: When the governing body decides to close or is ordered to close, it records the decision in minutes and gives the administrator written authority to carry out the Closure Plan the same day.

Verify the rule: Within 1 business day of the decision, the administrator reads the current Notice of Closure section of 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295 (Subpart B). The administrator writes the required notice deadlines to IDPH and to residents on page 1 of the Closure Plan, with the date verified and the administrator's initials.

Set the calendar: The administrator calculates the last permitted notice date for each recipient from the planned closure date. The administrator schedules all notices to go out no later than those dates, and earlier where possible.

Notify IDPH: The administrator sends the written closure notice to the IDPH Division of Assisted Living by the deadline in the rule. It states the closure date, the number of residents, and the relocation process. The administrator keeps a copy and proof of delivery in the Closure file.

Notify residents and representatives: The administrator delivers a written notice to each resident and each representative by the deadline in the rule. The notice includes the closure date, the reason, the relocation process, contact information for [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] at [PHONE], and how to reach the Ombudsman. Staff read or explain the notice to residents who cannot read it or who need language assistance (RTS-06). Each delivery is recorded on the Notice Log with date, method and recipient.

Notify the Ombudsman: On the same day that resident notices are issued, the administrator sends the Long-Term Care Ombudsman a copy of the notice and a list of affected residents, as permitted by RTS-05.

Notify other parties: The administrator notifies, through each resident's care team, hospice and home health agencies serving residents (CARE-07), arranged service providers, and each resident's physician of the closure date and each resident's relocation plan.

Individual relocation planning: Within [NUMBER] days of the notice, the administrator and the care/nurse designee meet with each resident and representative. They identify a receiving setting of the resident's choice that can meet the resident's needs. They use the current assessment and service plan (CARE-01) to confirm that the setting can do so.
Reasonable help: Staff help residents tour or contact receiving settings, arrange transportation (DL-02), and pack and move belongings. They record each step in the resident's record.

Transition of care: Before each move, the nurse designee prepares a transfer summary. It includes diagnoses, the current service plan, medication list and last administration times, diet, allergies, advance directives (RTS-03), physician contacts, and risk or behavior information. The summary is sent to the receiving setting with the resident, and the resident's medications are sent according to MED-01.

Weekly tracking: The administrator updates the Closure Plan weekly with each resident's status (setting identified, date of move, completed). Any resident without a confirmed placement is escalated to the governing body and the Ombudsman at once.

Staffing through closure: The administrator keeps staffing sufficient for the residents still in the building until the last resident has left (PER-01, PER-02). The 24-hour coverage rules continue to apply while any resident remains.

Funds and deposits: The business office reconciles each resident's account within [NUMBER] days after the move. It refunds prorated fees and deposits as the contract refund policy provides (CON-02), returns any resident funds held under CON-03, and gives the resident or representative a written final accounting.
Personal property: Staff inventory and return each resident's personal property at the move, with the resident or representative signing the inventory (CON-03).

Records: The administrator names a records custodian and a storage location in the Closure Plan. The resident records are kept, secured and made available for the periods required by REC-01. The custodian's name and contact details are given to IDPH and to former residents on request.
License and final steps: The administrator follows IDPH's instructions on return or surrender of the license (APP-01) and keeps final correspondence in the Closure file.
After-action: The governing body reviews the completed Closure Plan, and the Quality Improvement committee reviews any problems encountered (QI-01).

responsibilities.duty: Decides on closure, authorizes the Closure Plan, resolves unplaced residents, and ensures funds to carry out an orderly closure.
Leads relocation planning. Verifies the rule deadlines, sends all notices (IDPH, residents, representatives, Ombudsman), and keeps the Closure Plan and Notice Log.
Prepares transfer summaries, coordinates medications and care transitions, and meets residents and representatives.
Reconciles accounts, issues refunds and final accountings, and returns resident funds.
Secures and provides access to resident records after closure.

documentation: Governing body minutes authorizing closure
Closure Plan with verified notice deadlines and date of verification
Notice Log and copies of notices to IDPH, residents, representatives and the Ombudsman, with proof of delivery
Individual relocation plans and transfer summaries
Signed personal property inventories
Final account reconciliations and refund records
Records custodian designation and storage location

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2030 Establishment Contracts
policies.title: Assisted Living / Shared Housing Establishment Contract: Required Form and Content
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment; administrator, admissions staff, business office
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident signs a contract that has the required title and type size and contains every element required by 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2030, so that residents understand what they are agreeing to and IDPH can verify compliance.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] uses one standard contract form for all residents. This policy meets 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2030(a). The contract is titled "assisted living establishment contract" or "shared housing establishment contract," as applicable to our license, and is printed in no less than 12-point type. It contains all of the elements listed in 295.2030(a) in its body or in supporting documents or attachments. It specifically contains: (a)(1), the name, street address and mailing address of the establishment; (a)(4), the name and address of at least one natural person authorized to accept service on behalf of the owners and managing agent; (a)(5), a statement of the establishment's license status and of the license status of every provider of health-related or supportive services arranged by the establishment; and (a)(6), the duration of the contract. The contract also contains the other elements required by Section 295.2030 (including the base rate and services, extra services and fee schedule, the complaint process with notice of the Department on Aging Senior Helpline and the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program, the statement that Medicaid is not available, admission and termination criteria, a risk management statement, the list of resident rights under Section 95 of the Act, and the IDPH statement on the annual on-site review process). No resident will move in until the contract is signed by both parties. Fees, deposits, refunds, fee-change notice and emergency notification terms are covered in CON-02.

definitions.definition: The written agreement between the establishment and the resident (or representative) for residency and services.
The contract template approved by the governing body, verified against 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2030, and filed with IDPH (APP-02).
A natural person (not an entity) named in the contract who can accept legal papers for the owners and managing agent.
Documents such as the fee schedule, the rights list and the IDPH on-site review statement, that are attached and signed or acknowledged with the contract.

procedures: Title and type: The administrator ensures the contract's title reads exactly "assisted living establishment contract" or "shared housing establishment contract," matching the license type. The body and attachments are printed in at least 12-point type. The administrator checks a printed copy before each form revision is approved.

Maintain a content checklist: The administrator keeps a one-page checklist of every element required by 295.2030(a) and (b), copied from the current rule text, and records on it the contract section or attachment where each element appears. The checklist is re-verified against the rule at least annually and whenever the rule changes (GOV-01).
Establishment identification (a)(1): The form states the establishment's name, street address and mailing address exactly as on the license application: [ADDRESS].

Agent for service (a)(4): The form names at least one natural person and an address, currently [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] or another natural person designated by the owners, at [ADDRESS]. The administrator updates the form and notifies residents in writing within [NUMBER] days of any change.

License status (a)(5): The form states the establishment's license type and number, and lists every provider of health-related or supportive services (e.g., home health, hospice, therapy, pharmacy) arranged by us, with each provider's license status. The administrator verifies each provider's license before listing it and updates the list when providers change (CARE-07).
Duration (a)(6): The form states the contract's term, and that it may renew automatically each year. Any change to the contract must be in writing and signed by both parties.

Other required elements: The form contains the base rate and services; extra services and fee schedule; the complaint process, with the Department on Aging Senior Helpline ([DEPARTMENT ON AGING SENIOR HELPLINE PHONE]) and the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program ([OMBUDSMAN PHONE]); admission and termination criteria consistent with RES-01 through RES-03 and TERM-01; a risk management statement consistent with NRA-01; the Section 95 rights list consistent with RTS-01; and the current IDPH statement on the annual on-site review process.

Medicaid statement: The form states that Medicaid under Articles V and VI of the Public Aid Code is not available for services in the establishment. If we participate in the HFS Supportive Living Program, the SLP terms are handled under GOV-03 and do not replace this statement.
Fee terms: The form contains the occupancy, fee, deposit, refund, fee-change notice and emergency notification terms described in CON-02.

Explain before signing: Before signature, admissions staff review the contract with the resident and representative in plain language, with interpretation or accommodation when needed (RTS-06). They allow time for questions and for the resident to consult family, an attorney or the Ombudsman.

Signatures: The resident or representative and an authorized establishment agent sign and date the contract. Admissions staff verify that every page, blank and attachment is complete before signature.

Copies: Admissions staff give a complete copy of the signed contract and attachments to the resident or representative on the day of signing and note the date on the Contract Checklist. The original signed contract is kept on the premises in the resident's record (REC-01).

Changes and renewal: Any amendment is written, explains what is changing, and is signed by both parties before taking effect. The administrator diarizes each annual renewal date and confirms that the contract and attachments in use remain current.
IDPH copy: The administrator provides the standard contract form to IDPH as described in APP-02 and sends any revised form when the form changes.

Quarterly audit: The administrator audits a sample of at least [NUMBER] resident contracts quarterly against the checklist, corrects any gaps, and reports results to the Quality Improvement committee (QI-01).

responsibilities.duty: Approves the standard contract form and any revisions.
Maintains the content checklist, verifies license information, signs for the establishment, and sends the form to IDPH.
Explain the contract, obtain signatures, give copies, and file the signed original in the record.
Ensures that billing matches the contract fee schedule and that renewals and amendments are tracked.

documentation: Approved standard contract form (current version and version history)
295.2030 content checklist with verification dates
Signed contract and attachments in each resident's record
Contract Checklist showing the date a copy was given to the resident or representative
List of arranged service providers and their license verification
Quarterly contract audit results

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2030 Establishment Contracts
policies.title: Fees, Deposits, Refunds, Fee-Change Notice and Emergency Notification
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment; administrator, admissions staff, business office, nursing/care staff
policies.purpose: To make sure that each resident's contract clearly states the terms of occupancy, every fee, charge and deposit, the refund policy, how much notice is given before fees change, and how a relative or other designated person is notified of emergencies, significant changes in condition, and termination of residency.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] includes in every contract the terms required by 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2030(b), and follows them in practice.
