Personnel files are kept in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system. Only the Administrator, the human resources designee and others the Administrator authorizes can open them. Social Security numbers are never shown on schedules, badges or posted lists.
Files are kept available for review by IDPH surveyors during an inspection. Staff do not remove or alter documents to prepare for a survey.

Files of former employees are kept for the entire period of employment plus at least 12 months after the last date of employment or service. The designee records a 'destroy-after' date on each closed file.

Before any file is destroyed, the Administrator confirms that no law, payer requirement, pending claim, audit or investigation requires a longer period. Destruction is by shredding or secure deletion, and the date is logged.

Contract and agency workers who provide service in the establishment are subject to the same age, qualification, background check and file requirements, and [AGENCY NAME] keeps the same documentation for them.

responsibilities.duty: Approves job descriptions, confirms qualifications before hire, audits files and authorizes access and destruction.
Opens and maintains files, completes the checklist, tracks dates and keeps retention records.
Provide accurate personal information and current documents, and report changes in address, phone and certifications.
Approves the personnel record system and reviews audit results.

documentation: Signed job descriptions with minimum education and experience
Hiring checklist showing qualification and age verification
Personnel file for each employee with the items required by 295.3000(e) and (f)
Personnel File Checklist with audit dates and Administrator initials
Closed-file log with the last date of employment and destroy-after date
Record destruction log

policies.category: Subpart C – Personnel: § 295.3000 Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
policies.title: Nurse Aide Registry, Health Care Worker Background Checks and License Verification
policies.applies_to: Administrator, human resources designee and all hiring staff of [AGENCY NAME]; all applicants and employees with or who may have resident contact
policies.purpose: To keep people with substantiated findings of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property, people disqualified under the Health Care Worker Background Check Act, and people without an active required license out of resident care.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] screens every applicant before hire. This policy meets 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000(m) and 295.3000(n).

295.3000(m) – Nurse Aide Registry: [AGENCY NAME] checks all applicants with the Nurse Aide Registry before hiring. [AGENCY NAME] does not hire anyone with a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property on the Registry.

295.3000(n) – License verification: Before employing anyone in a position that requires a State professional license, [AGENCY NAME] contacts the Illinois Department of Professional Regulation (now part of the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation, IDFPR) to verify that the license is active. A copy of the verification is placed in the personnel file.

Health Care Worker Background Check Act: Every employee who has or may have resident contact must meet the Health Care Worker Background Check Act (225 ILCS 46). Compliance with the Act for covered employees is also a condition of licensure under 210 ILCS 9/35(a)(4). Fingerprints are collected electronically and sent to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days. [AGENCY NAME] applies the Act's rules on disqualifying offenses and waivers as in effect on the date of hire.

definitions.definition: The State registry that lists nurse aides and records any finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property against them.
A substantiated determination, entered on the Registry, of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property by the individual.

definitions.term: Health Care Worker Background Check Act
definitions.definition: 225 ILCS 46, which requires fingerprint-based checks and bars certain people with disqualifying convictions from employment in positions with resident contact, unless a waiver is granted as the Act allows.
Any position that requires a State professional license, such as a registered nurse or licensed practical nurse.

procedures: Before making any offer, the human resources designee runs the applicant's name on the Nurse Aide Registry. The designee prints or saves the result with the date and the designee's initials. This check is done for all applicants, not only those who say they are nurse aides.

If the Registry shows a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property, the applicant is not hired. The designee informs the Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], the same day and records the decision. The Registry result is kept confidential.
No one with resident contact begins work until the Registry check is complete and filed. If the Registry cannot be reached, the hire is delayed until the check is done.

The designee starts the Health Care Worker Background Check Act process for each applicant who will have or may have resident contact, including part-time, contract, agency and volunteer staff who work in resident areas, using the forms and procedure required by the Act.

Fingerprints are collected electronically from the applicant. The designee confirms that the fingerprints are transmitted to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days. The date of collection and the date of transmission are written on the background check log.
The designee tracks every pending background check on the log. If the result is not back by [30] days, the designee follows up and reports the status to the Administrator.

No employee with resident contact works unsupervised with residents until the Administrator has confirmed in writing that the requirements of the Act are met for that person. Any limited work before completion is allowed only to the extent the Act permits, and the Administrator documents the basis and the supervision arrangement.

If the background check shows a disqualifying conviction, the Administrator does not hire or retain the person in a position with resident contact unless a waiver is granted under the Act. A waiver is documented in the file before work starts.

Before offering any position that requires a State professional license, the designee contacts IDFPR or uses its license lookup to confirm that the license is active and not suspended, revoked or restricted. The designee prints the verification with the date and the designee's initials and places it in the personnel file.
For licensed staff, the designee re-verifies the license before its expiration date and at least annually. The expiration date is entered on the license tracking log.
An employee whose license lapses or is disciplined must tell the Administrator immediately. The employee may not perform duties that require the license until the license is active again.
The Administrator rechecks the Nurse Aide Registry for every direct care employee at least [annually] and whenever a concern about the employee's conduct arises. Re-checks are dated and filed.

If an employee is found to have a Registry finding, a disqualifying conviction or an inactive required license, the Administrator removes the employee from resident contact at once, reviews resident safety, and reports as required by RTS-02 and the Department's rules.

The Administrator audits the files of all new hires each quarter to confirm that the Registry check, background check compliance and license verification (if applicable) are on file and dated before the start date. Results go to the quality improvement program (QI-01).

responsibilities.duty: Decides on hire; confirms compliance with the Act before unsupervised resident contact; handles disqualifications and waivers.
Runs Registry and license checks, starts fingerprinting, maintains the logs and files all results.
Maintain an active license and report any lapse, restriction or discipline immediately.
Supports the Administrator's refusal to hire disqualified applicants and reviews audit findings.

documentation: Dated Nurse Aide Registry check for every applicant and the periodic re-checks
Health Care Worker Background Check Act forms, fingerprint collection and transmission dates, and results
Background check log showing dates and status
Written Administrator confirmation of compliance with the Act before unsupervised resident contact
License verification printout or confirmation for licensed positions, with initials and date
License expiration tracking log
Waiver documents, if any
Quarterly new-hire file audit results

policies.category: Subpart C – Personnel: § 295.3000 Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
policies.title: Manager / Director Qualifications, Training and Manager Changes
policies.applies_to: Governing Body, Administrator/Manager and any acting or relief manager of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is always led by a manager or director who meets the Act's qualifications, completes required training, and that IDPH is told promptly when the manager changes.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] employs a full-time director/manager who meets the qualifications of the Assisted Living and Shared Housing Act (210 ILCS 9/35(a)(2)): at least 21 years of age, with a high school diploma or equivalent, plus qualifying experience as defined in the job description (see PER-03). As a condition of licensure, the director completes at least 20 hours of training every 2 years (210 ILCS 9/35). If [AGENCY NAME] has a special dementia program, the director also receives dementia training (210 ILCS 9/150).

Public Act 104-0589 amended Section 35 of the Act. The Governing Body reviews the current text of Section 35 and the Department's rules on manager qualifications at each annual policy review and before any hire, and updates this policy if the requirements differ.

When the manager changes, [AGENCY NAME] reports the change to IDPH within 10 working days. If [AGENCY NAME] is a shared housing establishment, one manager may oversee up to three establishments only if they are within 30 minutes' drive of each other and the manager is immediately reachable, as the Department's rules allow.

definitions.definition: The full-time person responsible for day-to-day operation of the establishment and for carrying out the Governing Body's policies. Also called the Administrator in this manual.
The minimum experience stated in the director's written job description, as required by the Act and approved by the Governing Body.
The manager can be contacted at any time by phone and can respond to the building promptly. For a multi-site shared housing manager, this means arriving within the 30-minute limit.

procedures: Before hiring or promoting any manager, the Governing Body compares the candidate's age, education and experience with the Act's requirements and the written job description. Proof of age and a diploma or equivalent are copied into the personnel file.
The Governing Body confirms that the candidate meets the Health Care Worker Background Check Act and Nurse Aide Registry requirements before the candidate starts (see PER-04).
The Governing Body confirms that the director is full-time. The manager's schedule, job description and employment agreement state a full-time commitment.

At hire, the Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], completes a 2-year training plan listing at least 20 hours of training to be done in each 2-year period. The plan covers topics related to the operation of the establishment, such as resident rights, assessment and service planning, dementia care, abuse prevention, infection control, medication safety, emergency preparedness and management of staff.

The Administrator records each training in the training log: date, topic, hours, provider and certificate. A copy of the certificate is placed in the personnel file. Only documented hours are counted.

The human resources designee reviews the log every 6 months. If fewer than the hours needed are on track to be completed, the designee tells the Governing Body, and training is scheduled so that 20 hours are completed within each 2-year period.

If [AGENCY NAME] offers an Alzheimer's or dementia special care program, the director completes dementia training before the program opens or before the director takes on the program, and then at the intervals set by CARE-04.

The Governing Body names an on-site person in charge for each absence of the manager and gives that person a written list of duties and contact numbers. The manager remains reachable by phone during absences.

If a shared housing manager is to oversee more than one establishment, the Governing Body documents, before the arrangement starts, that no more than three establishments are involved, that each is within 30 minutes' drive, that the manager is immediately reachable, and that on-site staff are present in each building at all times as required by PER-02.

If the manager resigns, is terminated or is replaced, the Governing Body immediately appoints a qualified interim manager who meets the same qualifications. The establishment is not left without a manager.

Within 10 working days of the change, the Governing Body or its designee sends IDPH written notice of the manager change. The notice includes the former manager's name and last day, the new manager's name, start date and qualifications, and a contact telephone number of [PHONE]. A copy of the notice and proof of delivery are filed.

If there is an operational impact from the change, such as updated staff contact lists, the Administrator also updates the posted contact list, the disaster plan contacts (DIS-01), the license-related records (APP-01) and notifies residents and their representatives as described in the resident contract.

At each annual policy review (GOV-01), the Governing Body re-checks the current Section 35 text, any new Department rule on director qualifications and training hours, and this policy's 10-working-day reporting and multi-site provisions, and records the result in the minutes.

responsibilities.duty: Hires and supervises the manager, verifies qualifications, reports manager changes to IDPH within 10 working days and reviews the law at each annual review.
Maintains the 2-year training plan, completes and documents at least 20 hours of training every 2 years and stays reachable.
Keeps qualification documents and training certificates in the file and flags training shortfalls.
Meets the same qualifications and carries out the manager's duties until a permanent manager is in place.

documentation: Manager's proof of age, education and qualifying experience
Written job description and full-time employment agreement
2-year training plan and training log with certificates showing at least 20 hours per 2 years
Dementia training record (if a dementia program is offered)
Multi-site shared housing documentation (if applicable)
Written notice to IDPH of any manager change, with proof of delivery and date
Governing Body minutes showing review of Section 35 and this policy

policies.category: Subpart C – Personnel: § 295.3000 Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
policies.title: Employee Orientation and Ongoing Training
policies.applies_to: All employees of [AGENCY NAME], including direct care, dietary, housekeeping, maintenance and administrative staff, and contract and agency workers who serve residents
policies.purpose: To make sure every employee is oriented before working with residents and takes part in ongoing training that matches the needs of the people living here.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] provides orientation to every new employee and ongoing training to all staff. Staff take part in ongoing training that prepares them to serve the resident population (77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000(a); 210 ILCS 9/35(a)(3)). Orientation and in-service topics and hours meet or exceed those in the Department's orientation and training rules, which the Administrator keeps on file in a current Training Requirements List.

If [AGENCY NAME] offers a special dementia program, the director and direct care staff receive dementia training (210 ILCS 9/150; see CARE-04).

Bloodborne pathogen training under the OSHA standard (29 CFR 1910.1030) is given to every employee who has occupational exposure risk, at hire and at least annually thereafter.

Orientation and ongoing training are documented in each employee's file, as required by 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000(e)(2) (see PER-03).

definitions.definition: Initial instruction given to a new employee on [AGENCY NAME]'s policies, resident rights, emergency procedures and the employee's duties, before the employee works unsupervised with residents.
Continuing education given to current employees to keep skills current and to respond to the needs of the resident population.
Reasonably anticipated contact with blood or other potentially infectious materials while doing one's job, as defined in 29 CFR 1910.1030.

procedures: The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], keeps a Training Requirements List that states the orientation and in-service topics and the hours required by the Department's rules, plus [AGENCY NAME]'s own additions. The list is checked against the current rule at each annual policy review.

Each year the Administrator prepares an annual training calendar based on the Training Requirements List, the results of resident assessments, incident trends, survey findings and quality improvement results (QI-01).
Every new employee completes orientation before working unsupervised with residents. Orientation is led by the Administrator or a trained designee using the written Orientation Checklist.

Orientation includes at least: resident rights and the grievance process (RTS-01, RTS-04); abuse, neglect and exploitation recognition and mandatory reporting (RTS-02); privacy and confidentiality (RTS-05); fire safety, evacuation and disaster procedures (PP-03, DIS-01); infection control and hand hygiene (CARE-03); emergency response and change-of-condition reporting (CARE-05); the employee's job description and the service delivery plans of residents the employee will assist; and the policies on elopement (SAF-01) and restraints (SAF-02).

Direct care staff orientation also covers dignity in personal care, safe transfers, falls and skin integrity (CARE-06), medication reminder and assistance limits (MED-01) and the dementia needs of residents if a special dementia program is offered (CARE-04).

Within the first week of hire, each employee with exposure risk receives bloodborne pathogen training that meets 29 CFR 1910.1030. The training covers the exposure control plan, universal precautions, personal protective equipment, handling sharps and waste, and what to do after an exposure. A trainer is available to answer questions.

New direct care staff work with an experienced employee for [number of] shifts before working independently. The trainer signs off on each competency, such as transfers and personal care, on the competency checklist.
The employee and trainer both sign and date the Orientation Checklist when orientation is complete. The checklist is filed in the personnel file (295.3000(e)(2)(B)).
The Administrator schedules in-service training throughout the year at no cost to the employee, during paid work time. Staff who miss a session complete a make-up session within [30] days.

Annual training for all staff includes refreshers on resident rights, abuse and neglect reporting, infection control, emergency and disaster procedures, fire safety, bloodborne pathogens and any topic required by the Department's rules.

Where a special dementia program is offered, the director and all direct care staff receive dementia training before working with those residents and on a regular schedule set in CARE-04, covering topics such as communication, behavior, wandering and evacuation safety, and cognitive stimulation.
Training is also given when a new resident need, equipment, policy or survey finding requires it. The Administrator documents the topic, date, trainer, hours and attendees on a sign-in sheet.
Each employee's training record is updated after every session and kept in the personnel file (295.3000(e)(2)(C)). Certificates from outside trainers are copied into the file.

The human resources designee reviews the training log every quarter and lists employees who are behind. The Administrator makes sure those employees complete missing training before the next quarter ends.
The Administrator reports training completion rates and gaps to the Governing Body at least annually and uses them to improve the training plan.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the Training Requirements List and the annual calendar; delivers or arranges orientation and in-service training; ensures records are complete.
Teach and sign off competencies and report concerns about a new employee's readiness.
Tracks training completion and files records.
Attend and complete required training and apply what they learn.
Provides resources for training and reviews completion rates.

documentation: Current Training Requirements List
Annual training calendar
Completed Orientation Checklist signed by employee and trainer
Competency checklists for direct care staff
Sign-in sheets, training outlines and certificates
Bloodborne pathogen training records and exposure control plan
Dementia training records, if applicable
Training completion report to the Governing Body

policies.category: Subpart C – Personnel: § 295.3000 Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
policies.title: Employee Health Evaluation and TB Screening
policies.applies_to: All employees of [AGENCY NAME], especially direct care and food service employees, and the Administrator and human resources designee
policies.purpose: To protect residents and staff from communicable disease by making sure employees are healthy enough for their duties, free of pulmonary tuberculosis, and kept away from residents when they have a reportable or contagious illness.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] requires an initial health evaluation for direct care and food service employees. The timing and content of the evaluation, and the steps and timing of tuberculosis (TB) skin testing, follow the Department's rules in effect on the hire date. The Administrator keeps a current copy of those rules and a Health Screening Procedure derived from them, and checks them at each annual policy review.

The file of every employee must contain documentation of freedom from pulmonary tuberculosis (77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000(e)(2)(A)). The file of every direct care employee must also contain the initial health evaluation (77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000(f)(2)).

Employees who are ill with a communicable disease are excluded from resident contact and food handling as described in CARE-03. Employees with occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials are protected under the OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard (29 CFR 1910.1030).

definitions.definition: A documented health assessment by a licensed health care professional showing the employee is physically able to perform the job and is free of communicable disease.
Documentation, such as a negative TB test result or, if the test is positive, a clinical evaluation and chest x-ray result showing no active disease, as required by the Department's rules.
An employee who provides hands-on care or services to residents.
An employee who prepares, serves or handles food or food-contact surfaces for residents.

procedures: The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], keeps the Health Screening Procedure, which states the evaluation content, the TB test steps and timing, and re-screening intervals under the Department's rules. The procedure is checked against the current rule at each annual policy review.
The offer letter for any direct care or food service position states that employment depends on completing the health evaluation and TB screening.

Before the employee begins resident contact or food preparation, the human resources designee collects an initial health evaluation signed and dated by a physician, physician assistant, advanced practice registered nurse or other licensed health care professional allowed by the rules. The evaluation states the employee is able to perform the essential duties of the job and is free of communicable disease.

Before the employee begins work, the designee also collects documentation of freedom from pulmonary tuberculosis, completed according to the TB testing steps and timing in the Health Screening Procedure. For employees who test positive on a previous test, the designee collects documentation of the clinical evaluation, chest x-ray result and any treatment as required.

The designee reviews the documents for completeness: employee name, date, signature, credentials of the examiner and result. Incomplete documents are returned to the employee, and the employee does not start work until corrected.
An employee who has had a recent screening from a previous employer may use it only if it meets the current rule and [AGENCY NAME]'s procedure. The Administrator decides and documents the decision.

The designee files the health evaluation and TB documentation in the personnel file. Health information is kept in a separate confidential section of the file, available only to the Administrator, the designee and others authorized by law.

The designee enters the dates for any repeat TB screening or other required follow-up on the tracking log and tells the employee 30 days before each due date. An employee who does not complete a required rescreening by the due date is removed from resident contact and food handling until the documentation is received.

Employees must tell the Administrator before working if they have symptoms such as a persistent cough, fever, night sweats, unexplained weight loss, a new rash, vomiting, diarrhea or any diagnosed contagious condition. The Administrator decides whether the employee may work and for how long, following CARE-03.

An employee with symptoms of active TB is sent home immediately, is not allowed to return until cleared in writing by a health care provider or the local health department, and any reportable exposure is handled under CARE-03.

Residents' and staff exposures are evaluated with the local health department when a case of active TB or other reportable disease is found, and the Administrator keeps records of the contact investigation.

Employees with occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials are offered hepatitis B vaccination and post-exposure evaluation as provided in the establishment's exposure control plan under 29 CFR 1910.1030.

Employees with job-related restrictions on their health evaluation, such as a lifting limit, are assigned only to duties within those limits. The Administrator documents the restriction and the accommodation.

The Administrator audits the files of all new direct care and food service hires within 30 days of the start date to confirm the evaluation and TB documentation are present, dated and complete. Gaps are corrected immediately and reported in the quality improvement program (QI-01).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the Health Screening Procedure, decides whether ill employees may work and audits compliance.
Collects and files evaluations and TB documentation, tracks re-screening due dates and protects confidentiality.
Complete the evaluation and TB screening on time and report symptoms, exposures and diagnoses before working.
Send symptomatic employees home and tell the Administrator.

documentation: Health Screening Procedure derived from the current Department rules
Initial health evaluation for each direct care and food service employee
Documentation of freedom from pulmonary TB in every employee file
TB re-screening tracking log
Records of employee illness, exclusion and return-to-work clearance
Exposure and incident records and post-exposure evaluations
New-hire file audit results

policies.category: Subpart C – Personnel: § 295.3000 Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractors, volunteers and students who work at [AGENCY NAME], including direct care, dietary, housekeeping, maintenance, management and administrative staff.
policies.purpose: To protect residents from abuse, neglect, exploitation and misappropriation of property. To keep relationships between staff and residents professional. To make sure no one with a Nurse Aide Registry finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation is employed, as required by 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000(m).
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] has zero tolerance for abuse, neglect, financial exploitation and misappropriation of resident property. Staff may not accept gifts, loans or financial transactions from residents. Every employee signs a written Code of Conduct at hire and again at each annual review. [AGENCY NAME] does not employ anyone who has a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property on the Illinois Health Care Worker Registry (Nurse Aide Registry), consistent with 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000(m). Any violation of this policy that involves abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported under RTS-02 (Abuse, Neglect and Financial Exploitation Prevention and Reporting). Violations are grounds for discipline up to and including termination. This policy has no official checklist items assigned.

definitions.definition: Any physical injury, sexual abuse, verbal or emotional abuse, or willful deprivation of care or services that causes, or could cause, harm to a resident.
A failure to provide the care, supervision or services a resident needs and that are in the service plan, resulting in harm or risk of harm.
Taking, using, borrowing or controlling a resident's money, property or benefits without the resident's informed consent, or by deception, coercion or undue influence.
The limit that keeps the staff-resident relationship focused on the resident's care and protects the resident from personal, financial or sexual involvement with staff.
The check of the Illinois Health Care Worker Registry for a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property, completed before hire.

procedures: Before any job offer becomes final, the Administrator or designee completes the Nurse Aide Registry check and records the date, result and the name of the person who ran it in the employee file (see PER-04). The Administrator does not hire anyone with a registry finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property.
On the first day of work, before any resident contact, each new employee reads and signs the [AGENCY NAME] Code of Conduct. The signed copy goes in the employee file, and the employee gets a copy.

The Code of Conduct states that staff must never abuse, neglect, threaten, humiliate, restrain without authority, or exploit any resident. It also states that staff must not take, borrow or use resident property or money.

Staff may not accept gifts, loans, money, tips, bequests, or any financial transaction from a resident or the resident's family or representative. This includes buying or selling items, borrowing or lending money, being named on a resident's accounts, and handling a resident's cash or cards for personal purposes. Staff may not ask residents for any such item.

If a resident offers a gift, the employee politely declines and explains that the rule protects residents. If the resident would be hurt by a refusal, the employee takes the item only to give it to the Administrator, who documents it and returns it to the resident or representative with an explanation. A card or thank-you note is allowed.

Resident funds and property are handled only as described in CON-03 (Resident Funds and Personal Property). Staff who shop or run errands for a resident keep receipts and return change and receipts to the resident, with a witness signature when possible.

Staff may not enter into romantic or sexual relationships with residents, share personal problems or finances with residents, or use residents' personal items. Staff do not give out home addresses or personal phone numbers to residents.
Staff may not post, photograph, record or share any resident's image, name or information on social media or personal devices (see RTS-05).
Staff may not work under the influence of alcohol or unlawful drugs, and may not bring weapons onto the premises.
Staff may not use physical or chemical restraint, seclusion or any restrictive practice except as allowed under SAF-02.

Any employee who sees, suspects or hears of a violation of this policy, including abuse, neglect, exploitation, misappropriation or a gift or loan, must tell the Administrator immediately. If the Administrator is involved, the employee contacts [GOVERNING BODY CONTACT]. The employee also follows the reporting steps in RTS-02, including notice to the authorities that RTS-02 requires.
Retaliation against anyone who reports in good faith is prohibited. The Administrator tells every employee this in orientation and documents it.
The Administrator immediately protects any resident at risk. An employee accused of abuse, neglect or exploitation is removed from resident contact until the investigation is complete.
The Administrator investigates, starting the same day, and documents the facts, interviews, findings and action taken. Findings are reported as RTS-02 and INC-01 require.

Violations of this policy lead to corrective action up to termination. Substantiated abuse, neglect or misappropriation is reported to the agencies that RTS-02 identifies, including the Health Care Worker Registry where required.
The Administrator reviews the Code of Conduct with all staff at least annually during ongoing training (PER-06) and documents attendance and signatures.

responsibilities.duty: Runs the registry check before hire, has the Code of Conduct signed, investigates reports, protects residents and applies discipline.
Model professional conduct, watch for boundary problems and report concerns the same day.
Follow the Code of Conduct, refuse gifts and loans, and report any suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately.
Receives reports involving the Administrator and makes sure complaints are investigated.

documentation: Signed Code of Conduct in each employee file (hire and annual re-signing)
Nurse Aide Registry check result with date and verifier
Records of any gift offered, declined or turned over to the Administrator
Investigation file and corrective action records
Training attendance records on this policy

policies.category: Subpart D – Resident Care and Services (§ 295.4000–295.4060)
policies.title: Pre-Admission Comprehensive Assessment, Reassessment and Service Plan
policies.applies_to: All prospective and current residents; the Administrator, nursing and direct care staff, and the physician, physician assistant or advanced practice registered nurse who completes assessments.
policies.purpose: To make sure each resident has a physician, PA or APRN comprehensive assessment before admission, and repeated assessments and a written service plan that match the resident's needs. This follows 210 ILCS 9/15, as amended by Public Act 104-0589, and 210 ILCS 9/150.
policies.policy: Before admission, a comprehensive assessment of the prospective resident's physical, cognitive and psychosocial condition is completed by a physician, physician assistant or advanced practice registered nurse (210 ILCS 9/15, as amended by Public Act 104-0589). A registered nurse or licensed practical nurse may not complete this comprehensive assessment. The assessment is repeated at least annually and whenever there is a significant change in condition, including a diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease or a related dementia. Pre-admission assessment tools must be validated for dementia-related cognitive impairment (210 ILCS 9/150(g)). A written service plan is agreed by [AGENCY NAME], the resident and the resident's representative, and is reviewed at least annually and whenever needs change. On request, the resident or representative receives a copy of the latest assessment, any supplemental establishment assessment, and the service plan. Public Act 104-0589 shows an effective date of July 24, 2026. [AGENCY NAME] confirms the effective date against the Public Act text and follows the amended requirement as soon as it is in force. If the older rule wording refers to a physician, the Administrator reconciles that wording with the Act and, until the conflict is resolved, uses a physician or obtains written direction from IDPH. This policy has no official checklist items assigned.

definitions.definition: The assessment of a person's physical, cognitive and psychosocial condition completed by a physician, PA or APRN before admission, annually, and on significant change.
Any additional assessment [AGENCY NAME] completes (for example by a nurse) to plan care. It does not replace the comprehensive assessment.
The written plan of services mutually agreed by the establishment, the resident and the representative.
A major decline or improvement in physical, cognitive or psychosocial status, or a new diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease or a related dementia, that is likely to change the resident's service needs.
The person the resident has named or who is legally authorized to act for the resident (see RTS-03).

procedures: The Administrator or designee gives each applicant a request form for the comprehensive assessment and sends it to the applicant's physician, PA or APRN, or arranges an assessment by one of these providers. The Administrator documents the provider's name, license type and number, and date.

The Administrator checks that the assessor is a physician, PA or APRN. An assessment signed only by an RN, LPN or other staff member is not accepted as the comprehensive assessment and must be redone.
The assessment must address physical, cognitive and psychosocial condition. The Administrator reviews it for completeness before the admission decision. Missing sections are returned to the assessor.

For applicants who have or may have dementia, the cognitive section must use a tool validated for dementia-related cognitive impairment (210 ILCS 9/150(g)). Follow CARE-04 for the dementia-specific tool and signature requirements.
The Administrator completes the admission decision under RES-01 and RES-02 only after the assessment is in hand. No resident moves in before the assessment is complete and reviewed.

A nurse or other qualified staff member may complete a supplemental establishment assessment, including skin-integrity and nutrition screening (see CARE-06 and FOOD-01), to plan services. It is kept with the comprehensive assessment.

Within [7] days before or on the day of admission, the Administrator or nurse meets with the resident and representative to develop the written service plan. It lists the services the resident needs, who will provide them, how often, and the resident's preferences.
The plan is signed by the resident or representative and by [AGENCY NAME]. Disagreements are recorded and discussed, and the resident's right to refuse services is respected (see RTS-01 and NRA-01).
The Administrator schedules each resident's annual comprehensive assessment at least 30 days before the one-year anniversary of the last assessment and tracks due dates on the assessment log.

Staff report a significant change in condition to the nurse or Administrator the same day (see CARE-05). The Administrator requests a new comprehensive assessment by the physician, PA or APRN promptly, within [14] days of the change, and sooner if safety requires.
A new diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease or a related dementia always triggers a new comprehensive assessment and a service plan review.
When IDPH sets more frequent skin-integrity or nutrition assessments by rule, the Administrator adds them to the assessment schedule and gives staff written instructions on the frequency in effect.

The service plan is reviewed with the resident and representative at least annually and whenever needs change, including after hospitalization and after each new comprehensive assessment. Changes are signed and dated.

On request, the Administrator gives the resident or representative a copy of the latest comprehensive assessment, any supplemental establishment assessment, and the current service plan. Requests are logged, and the copies are supplied promptly, normally within [2] business days.
The Administrator updates and distributes the plan to direct care staff after each change, and staff sign that they have read it.
The Administrator reviews the assessment log monthly and reports overdue assessments to the governing body.

responsibilities.duty: Completes the pre-admission, annual and change-of-condition comprehensive assessments and signs them.
Verifies the assessor and the assessment, decides on admission, schedules reassessments and keeps the assessment log.
Completes supplemental assessments, helps write the service plan and identifies changes in condition.
Follow the service plan, report changes and record services given.
Take part in developing and agreeing to the service plan and may request copies of records.

documentation: Pre-admission comprehensive assessment signed by a physician, PA or APRN, with credentials
Annual and change-of-condition assessments
Supplemental establishment assessments
Signed and dated service plan and every revision
Assessment due-date log
Log of record copy requests and dates provided
Record of reconciliation of rule and Act wording and of the effective-date confirmation

policies.category: Subpart D – Resident Care and Services (§ 295.4000–295.4060)
policies.title: Mandatory and Optional Services Offered
policies.applies_to: Administrator, nursing and direct care staff, and the person who completes the license application and the establishment contract.
policies.purpose: To define the mandatory and optional services [AGENCY NAME] provides, and to make sure the list is sent to IDPH with the license application and stated in the resident contract.
policies.policy: This policy meets 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.500(a)(10), Information about the mandatory and optional services to be provided at the establishment. [AGENCY NAME] provides every service the IDPH rule lists as mandatory. It also offers the optional services listed in Attachment B, each with its fee. The Administrator keeps a written list of mandatory and optional services, submits it to IDPH with the license application, and includes it in the establishment contract (77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2030). Services may be provided directly by [AGENCY NAME] or arranged with others, with the resident's consent (210 ILCS 9/70). Medication reminders, supervision of self-administered medication and medication administration are defined in 210 ILCS 9/70 and carried out as MED-01 and MED-02 describe. The Administrator prepares Attachment A (mandatory services) directly from the current text of the IDPH rule, since the rule text is not reproduced here.

definitions.definition: A service that IDPH rule requires every establishment of this type to provide to residents.
A service [AGENCY NAME] chooses to offer, such as medication administration, for which a fee schedule is disclosed in the contract.
A service defined in 210 ILCS 9/70 in which a resident is reminded to take medication; see MED-01.
Oversight of a resident taking his or her own medication, performed under a licensed health care professional, or under RN delegation for a certified medication aide (210 ILCS 9/70).

Giving medication to a resident, performed by a licensed health care professional employed by the establishment, or by a certified medication aide under RN supervision and delegation within the limits in 210 ILCS 9/70.
A service provided by an outside provider that the establishment helps the resident obtain, with the resident's consent.

procedures: Before filing the license application, the Administrator obtains the current text of the IDPH rule on mandatory services and prepares Attachment A, listing each mandatory service, who provides it, and how it is delivered at [AGENCY NAME].

The Administrator and governing body decide which optional services [AGENCY NAME] will offer and list them on Attachment B. Medication administration, if offered, is described with the staff who perform it (a licensed health care professional employed by the establishment, or a certified medication aide under RN delegation within the limits in 210 ILCS 9/70).
The governing body sets a fee for each optional service. Fees are listed in the fee schedule in the contract (CON-01, CON-02).

The Administrator states, for each service, whether it is provided directly by staff or arranged with an outside provider, and names the provider where known. Arranged services are provided only with the resident's consent.
The Administrator submits Attachments A and B with the license application under APP-01, as 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.500(a)(10) requires, and keeps a copy of the submitted version.
The Administrator copies the same lists, base rate and extra-service fee schedule into the establishment contract, as 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2030 requires.
If [AGENCY NAME] does not offer medication administration, the Administrator tells applicants in writing before admission and follows the vaccine advice requirements in RES-03 and CARE-03.
Before admission, the Administrator reviews the service plan (CARE-01) against Attachments A and B and does not accept a resident whose needs [AGENCY NAME] cannot meet or arrange (RES-01, RES-02).
Direct care staff provide only the services listed in the service plan and within their training and legal scope. Nursing tasks are done only by licensed staff or delegated as MED-02 permits.
For arranged services, staff help the resident contact the provider, share needed information only with consent (RTS-05), and record the arrangement in the service plan.
The Administrator reviews Attachments A and B at least annually and whenever a service is added, removed or repriced, and updates the contract template and the IDPH submission as required.

When an optional service is added or its fee changes, the Administrator gives residents the written notice required by CON-02 (at least 30 days' written notice for fee changes, other than changes due to service needs in the service plan).

responsibilities.duty: Decides which optional services are offered and approves fees.
Prepares and updates Attachments A and B, files them with the license application, and makes sure the contract matches.
Oversees medication-related services and delegation as MED-01 and MED-02 describe.
Provide services listed in the service plan, within training and scope.

documentation: Attachment A: Mandatory services list
Attachment B: Optional services list with fees
Copy of the list submitted with the IDPH license application
Establishment contract showing services and fee schedule
Annual review record
Written resident consent for arranged services

policies.category: Subpart D – Resident Care and Services (§ 295.4000–295.4060)
policies.title: Communicable Disease, TB and Infection Prevention and Control
policies.applies_to: All staff, residents, volunteers and visitors at [AGENCY NAME]; the Administrator, nursing staff, housekeeping, laundry and dietary staff.
policies.purpose: To prevent and control the spread of communicable diseases, including tuberculosis, among residents and staff, to protect workers from bloodborne pathogens, and to ensure outbreaks are reported to public health authorities.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains written communicable disease and infection control procedures as the IDPH assisted living rules require. The Administrator keeps the IDPH rule text on communicable disease and tuberculosis screening on file, and these procedures are updated whenever the rule changes. Staff follow standard precautions with all residents. The establishment follows the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard (29 CFR 1910.1030) for any employee with occupational exposure. Staff health evaluation and TB screening are carried out under PER-07. If [AGENCY NAME] does not offer medication administration, it gives residents advice on pneumococcal and influenza vaccines as RES-03 and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000 require. Communicable disease outbreaks are reported as required by public health rules. Staffing must always be sufficient to carry out infection control duties (77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000(a)). This policy has no official checklist items assigned.

definitions.definition: Infection control practices used with all residents, including hand hygiene, gloves and other personal protective equipment, safe sharps handling and cleaning.
An illness that can be passed from one person to another, such as influenza, COVID-19, tuberculosis, norovirus, scabies or hepatitis.
Reasonably anticipated contact with blood or other potentially infectious material during an employee's duties.
Two or more cases of the same illness linked by time and place, or any number defined as reportable by public health authorities.

procedures: The Administrator designates an Infection Control Coordinator, [INFECTION CONTROL COORDINATOR NAME], who maintains this program, tracks illnesses and is the contact for public health authorities.
All staff complete infection control training at orientation and annually (PER-06): hand hygiene, standard precautions, PPE, cleaning, sharps, isolation and reporting. Attendance is documented.

Staff wash or sanitize hands before and after resident contact, before food handling, after toileting or glove removal, and whenever hands are soiled. Gloves, gowns and masks are worn when contact with blood, body fluids or infectious material is expected. PPE is stocked at [LOCATION].

The Administrator writes an Exposure Control Plan under 29 CFR 1910.1030 that identifies tasks with occupational exposure, provides PPE and sharps containers at no cost, offers hepatitis B vaccine to exposed employees, and sets post-exposure evaluation steps. It is reviewed annually.

After a needlestick or other exposure, the employee washes the site, reports to the Administrator immediately and receives medical evaluation. The Administrator records the incident in the exposure log and sharps injury log.

Staff health evaluation and TB screening before work and during employment follow PER-07. Resident TB screening follows the IDPH rule on TB skin tests, as shown on the admission checklist. The Administrator keeps results in the proper file, kept separate from the personnel and resident records.

A resident or employee with symptoms of a communicable disease is reported to the nurse or Administrator immediately. Employees with infectious illness are sent home or excluded from work until safe to return as directed by a health care provider or the health department.

Residents with suspected communicable disease are assessed, their physician is notified (CARE-05), and precautions are used as the physician or health department directs. [AGENCY NAME] arranges appropriate care or transfer if it cannot safely provide it (RES-01, RES-02).

The Infection Control Coordinator reports reportable diseases and suspected outbreaks to [LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT NAME AND PHONE] as public health rules require, and notifies IDPH as INC-01 requires where applicable. Staff cooperate fully with public health investigations.

During an outbreak, the Administrator may limit group activities, restrict visitors or use cohorting as public health authorities advise, while respecting resident and visitor rights (RTS-01, ESP-01). Residents and representatives are told promptly.

Housekeeping and laundry staff follow cleaning, disinfection and soiled-linen procedures under PP-02. Dietary staff follow food hygiene practices under FOOD-01, and staff with vomiting or diarrhea do not prepare food.
Medical waste and sharps are placed in puncture-resistant containers and disposed of by [WASTE CONTRACTOR] under applicable law. Medication disposal follows MED-01.

If [AGENCY NAME] does not provide medication administration, the nurse or Administrator gives each resident advice, in writing, on pneumococcal and influenza vaccines at admission and as RES-03 and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000 require. Staff record the advice and the resident's decision in the resident record.
The Infection Control Coordinator keeps a monthly line list of resident and staff infections, reviews it for patterns, and reports results to the Quality Improvement committee (QI-01).
The Administrator reviews this policy at least annually and after each outbreak.

responsibilities.duty: Oversees the program, assigns the Infection Control Coordinator, ensures supplies, training and reporting.
Tracks illnesses, reports to public health, and reviews practices and outbreaks.
Practice standard precautions, report symptoms and exposures, and complete training.
Follow cleaning, linen and food hygiene procedures.
Follow reasonable infection control measures such as hand hygiene and staying away when ill.

documentation: Written infection control and communicable disease procedures
Exposure Control Plan (29 CFR 1910.1030), exposure and sharps injury logs
Training records
Employee TB screening and health evaluation results (separate confidential file)
Monthly infection line list and outbreak reports
Reports to local health department and IDPH
Written vaccine advice given to residents and their decisions

policies.category: Subpart D – Resident Care and Services (§ 295.4000–295.4060)
policies.title: Alzheimer's Disease and Dementia Care Programs
policies.applies_to: Administrator, direct care and nursing staff, activity staff and anyone involved in the care of residents with Alzheimer's disease or related dementia at [AGENCY NAME].
policies.purpose: To make sure residents with dementia are assessed with an approved validated tool, are admitted and retained only when [AGENCY NAME] can provide appropriate care, and receive the safeguards that Illinois law requires of special dementia programs (210 ILCS 9/150; 210 ILCS 9/35(a)(7)).
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not admit or retain a resident when it cannot provide or secure appropriate care or lacks appropriately skilled staff (210 ILCS 9/150). Residency is also barred if the resident's condition has so deteriorated that residency is detrimental to the resident or others, or if the resident is dangerous and the danger cannot be eliminated. Dementia-related cognitive assessment uses the validated dementia-specific assessment standard identified in IDPH rule. It is approved by the physician, or by a PA or APRN with geriatric dementia experience. It is done before acceptance, annually, and on a change in condition. Annual and change-of-condition assessments must be signed by a physician. Where [AGENCY NAME] offers a special dementia program, it files the Alzheimer's and dementia special care disclosure document with its IDPH license application (210 ILCS 9/35(a)(7)) and discloses the program to IDPH and to residents. The program also meets the safeguards in 210 ILCS 9/150: a designated representative, wandering and evacuation safety policies, family communication, cognitive stimulation and activities, appropriate staffing, director and direct care staff dementia training, and emergency procedures and staffing patterns. The rule-level staffing and training numbers are taken from the IDPH rule in force. This policy has no official checklist items assigned.

definitions.definition: A program or unit that [AGENCY NAME] advertises or offers for residents with Alzheimer's disease or related dementia, which triggers the disclosure and program requirements of 210 ILCS 9/150.
The assessment standard identified by IDPH rule that has inter-rater reliability and is validated for dementia-related cognitive impairment.
A person identified for each resident with dementia who can make decisions and receive communications on the resident's behalf (see RTS-03).
The Alzheimer's and dementia special care disclosure document filed with IDPH and given to residents.

procedures: The governing body decides whether [AGENCY NAME] will offer a special dementia program and records the decision in its minutes (GOV-01). If it does not, the Administrator does not advertise one and applies the admission limits in this policy and RES-01 and RES-02.

If a program is offered, the Administrator completes the Alzheimer's and dementia special care disclosure document and files it with the IDPH license application (APP-01). The document is given to each prospective resident and representative before admission and kept in the resident record.
The Administrator obtains the name of the validated dementia-specific assessment tool IDPH has identified in rule, and records its source and version.

Before acceptance, the validated tool is used as part of the comprehensive assessment (CARE-01). The physician, or a PA or APRN with geriatric dementia experience, approves the assessment. The Administrator verifies the assessor's experience and keeps the verification.

The Administrator decides on admission only after reviewing the assessment, and declines or defers admission if [AGENCY NAME] cannot meet the person's needs with its staff and building, if the person is dangerous and the danger cannot be eliminated, or if residency would be detrimental to the person or others (RES-01, RES-02).

The assessment is repeated annually and on a change in condition (see CARE-05). The annual and change-of-condition assessments must be signed by a physician. Overdue assessments are tracked on the assessment log.

Each resident with dementia has a designated representative documented in the record before admission and updated when changes occur (RTS-03). Family and representatives are told how to reach staff and are invited to care planning meetings.
The Administrator coordinates family communication through at least [quarterly] updates, prompt calls about changes of condition, and an open-door policy for questions. Contacts are logged.

Residents with dementia have a service plan (CARE-01) that includes cognitive stimulation and individualized activities daily (DL-01), consistent routines, behavior support approaches and the resident's preferences and history.

Staffing patterns for the program are set in writing by the Administrator, based on resident acuity, time of day and the layout of the building, and meet or exceed the IDPH rule in force and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000. The pattern is attached to the disclosure document and reviewed at least quarterly (PER-01).

The Administrator and all direct care staff complete dementia training before working independently with residents and at least annually, in the number of hours the IDPH rule requires. Training content, trainer and dates are recorded (PER-05, PER-06).

Wandering and evacuation safety policies are in place under SAF-01 and PP-03. They address door alarms, supervision, ID bracelets or photos, search procedures and the evacuation of residents who cannot follow directions. Emergency procedures are practiced in drills (DIS-03).
Staff do not use physical or chemical restraints or other restrictive practices except as SAF-02 permits. Behaviors are managed through person-centered, non-drug approaches first.

The Administrator reviews the dementia program at least annually with the QI committee (QI-01), including falls, elopements, incidents, activity participation and family feedback, and updates the disclosure document if the program changes. Updates are given to IDPH and to residents.

responsibilities.duty: Decides whether to offer a special dementia program and approves staffing and budgets.
Files the disclosure document, verifies assessments, sets staffing and training, and decides on admission and retention.
Approves the validated assessment, and a physician signs annual and change-of-condition assessments.
Deliver individualized care and activities, follow wandering and safety procedures, and report changes.
Take part in care planning and receive communications about the resident.

documentation: Alzheimer's and dementia special care disclosure document as filed with IDPH
Validated dementia-specific assessments with assessor verification and physician signatures
Assessment due-date log
Designated representative record and family communication log
Program staffing pattern and quarterly reviews
Dementia training records for the Administrator and direct care staff
QI review of the dementia program

policies.category: Subpart D – Resident Care and Services (§ 295.4000–295.4060)
policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
policies.applies_to: All direct care and nursing staff, the Administrator, and any staff member who observes a change in a resident's condition at [AGENCY NAME].
policies.purpose: To make sure staff recognize and report changes in a resident's condition promptly, notify the physician and representative, obtain emergency care or hospital transfer when needed, and reassess the resident's needs and continued suitability for residency.
policies.policy: A significant change in a resident's condition triggers a new comprehensive assessment and a review of the service plan (210 ILCS 9/15). Staff report any change in condition to the nurse or Administrator immediately, and call 911 for an emergency. The resident's physician is notified, and the representative or designated person is notified under the emergency and relative notification policy in the resident contract (77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2030). After any change, the Administrator re-evaluates the resident against the retention criteria in 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000 to confirm that [AGENCY NAME] still has the staff and services to meet the resident's needs. A health or medical decline alone is not a reportable incident under the IDPH incident reporting rule, but any resulting serious harm is reportable (INC-01). Each notification is documented in the resident record. This policy has no official checklist items assigned.

definitions.definition: Any new or worsening sign, symptom, behavior, function loss, injury, fall, weight change, skin problem or cognitive or mood change that differs from the resident's usual status.
A change expected to alter the resident's service needs, including a major decline or improvement and a new diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease or related dementia.
A sudden condition that threatens life or health, such as chest pain, difficulty breathing, stroke signs, severe bleeding, unresponsiveness, a serious injury or a suspected overdose.
The representative or relative the resident has named, in the contract, to be notified of emergencies and changes.

procedures: Any staff member who notices a change in condition reports it immediately to the nurse on duty or the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] / person in charge, and documents objective observations (what was seen, when, vital signs where staff are trained and authorized to take them).

In an emergency, staff call 911 first, stay with the resident, give only first aid and CPR within training, follow the resident's advance directive or POLST if available (RTS-03), and then notify the Administrator.

For a non-emergency change, the nurse or Administrator contacts the resident's physician, PA or APRN the same day, by phone or [PORTAL], and gives the observations. Instructions received are written down and read back.

The nurse or Administrator notifies the representative or designated person under the notification policy in the resident's contract. For an emergency or transfer, this is done as soon as possible after 911 is called, and no later than [2 hours] after the event. For a non-emergency significant change, notice is given the same day.
If the representative cannot be reached, staff try each contact on the emergency contact list, record the times and numbers called, and keep trying. The attempts are recorded in the resident record.

When a resident is sent to the hospital, staff send a transfer packet with the resident's face sheet, current medication list, diagnoses, allergies, advance directive or POLST, physician and representative contacts, and a written description of the reason for transfer. A staff member or family member accompanies the resident where possible.

The Administrator or nurse calls the hospital within [24] hours to confirm admission and get an update, and keeps in contact with the representative. If the resident is discharged back, staff obtain the discharge orders, medication changes and follow-up instructions before or on the resident's return.

The Administrator determines whether the change is a significant change in condition. If so, the Administrator requests a new comprehensive assessment from a physician, PA or APRN (CARE-01) and schedules it promptly. For a new dementia diagnosis, the dementia procedures in CARE-04 also apply.

The nurse or Administrator reviews and revises the service plan with the resident and representative within [14] days of the change, or sooner if safety requires, and informs direct care staff of the changes in writing (CARE-01).
Staff follow up on falls, skin changes, weight loss and nutrition concerns under CARE-06 and FOOD-01, and on medication changes under MED-01 and MED-02.

After any significant change, after hospital return, and at each reassessment, the Administrator re-evaluates the resident against the criteria in 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000 and RES-01 and RES-02. The Administrator documents whether [AGENCY NAME] still has staff of the right number and skill, and can provide or secure the needed services.

If [AGENCY NAME] can no longer meet the resident's needs, the Administrator discusses options with the resident and representative, including added services or an outside provider, hospice (CARE-07), a negotiated risk agreement (NRA-01), or relocation. Any termination follows the notice rules in TERM-01.

The Administrator decides whether the event is a reportable serious incident or accident under INC-01. A decline alone is not reportable, but any serious harm resulting from it, such as an injury or death in circumstances covered by INC-01, is reported to IDPH as INC-01 requires.

Staff record every change in condition, physician contact, representative notification (with date, time, person told and by whom), transfer and follow-up in the resident record by the end of the shift (REC-01).
The nurse or Administrator reviews all changes in condition and transfers monthly for patterns and reports results to the Quality Improvement committee (QI-01).

responsibilities.duty: Notice and report changes immediately, call 911 in emergencies and document observations.
Assess, contact the physician, notify the representative, prepare the transfer packet and update the plan.
Ensures notification, requests reassessment, re-evaluates against residency criteria and decides on incident reporting.
Gives orders and performs the comprehensive reassessment after significant change.
Receives notification, takes part in service plan changes and makes decisions where authorized.

documentation: Change-of-condition note with date, time, observations and staff signature
Physician, PA or APRN contact record and orders
Representative notification record with date, time, person told and attempts made
Hospital transfer packet copy and transfer log
Updated comprehensive assessment and service plan
Written re-evaluation against 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000 criteria
Incident report if applicable (INC-01)

policies.category: Subpart D – Resident Care and Services (§ 295.4000–295.4060)
policies.title: Falls Prevention and Skin Integrity
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment – all direct care staff, nurses, the Administrator and the service plan team
policies.purpose: To reduce falls and pressure injuries among residents, to identify risk early, and to make sure [AGENCY NAME] does not accept or keep a resident whose skin condition is beyond what the establishment may lawfully serve.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] assesses every resident for fall risk and skin-integrity risk before admission, at least annually, and whenever the resident's condition changes significantly. Fall and skin risk and the agreed interventions are written into the resident's service plan under 210 ILCS 9/15. The pre-admission comprehensive assessment is completed by a physician, physician assistant or APRN as that Section requires, and it is repeated at least annually and on a significant change in condition. If IDPH sets more frequent skin-integrity or nutrition assessments by rule, [AGENCY NAME] will follow the more frequent schedule from the date the rule takes effect. [AGENCY NAME] will not retain a resident who needs treatment of a stage 3 or stage 4 decubitus ulcer (77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000(c)(12)). A fall that causes injury is a serious incident and is reported to IDPH within 24 hours under policy INC-01.

definitions.definition: An unintended event in which a resident comes to rest on the floor, ground or a lower surface, whether or not the fall is witnessed or causes injury.
A fall that results in any injury needing first aid beyond a bandage, evaluation by a health care professional, or transfer to a hospital. It is a serious incident reportable to IDPH within 24 hours.
The condition of the resident's skin, including redness, breakdown, pressure injuries, wounds and skin tears.

Localized damage to skin and underlying tissue caused by pressure. Stage 3 and stage 4 ulcers involve full-thickness tissue loss and are grounds for non-retention under 295.2000(c)(12) when treatment is needed.

A change in the resident's physical, cognitive or psychosocial status that requires a new comprehensive assessment under 210 ILCS 9/15. Examples are a fall with injury, a new skin wound, a new Alzheimer's or dementia diagnosis, or a hospital stay.

procedures: Before admission, the Administrator confirms that the physician, physician assistant or APRN comprehensive assessment includes fall history, mobility, balance, vision, continence, cognition, medications that raise fall risk, and skin condition. The assessment is obtained under CARE-01.

Before admission, a licensed nurse or other qualified staff member named by the Administrator reviews the assessment and checks the resident's skin on arrival. The skin check is recorded on the [AGENCY NAME] Admission Skin Check form.

If the assessment or skin check shows a stage 3 or stage 4 decubitus ulcer needing treatment, the Administrator does not admit the resident. The Administrator documents the reason and follows RES-01 and RES-02. For a current resident, the Administrator starts the termination and relocation process under TERM-01.

The service plan team (resident, representative, Administrator and nurse) records fall risk, skin risk and agreed interventions in the written service plan. The plan is signed by the provider, the resident and the representative under CARE-01.

Staff carry out the interventions in the service plan. Examples are walking aids within reach, call access, non-slip footwear, clear walkways, adequate lighting, scheduled toileting, repositioning prompts, and nutrition and hydration support coordinated with FOOD-01.
The Maintenance Lead inspects hallways, bathrooms, stairs, floors and lighting weekly. Hazards are corrected or isolated the same day and logged in the Maintenance Log (PP-02).

Direct care staff observe the resident's skin during bathing, dressing and personal care. Any new redness, breakdown, wound or skin tear is reported to the nurse or Administrator before the end of the shift.

The nurse examines the area within 24 hours of the report and documents its location, size and appearance. The nurse notifies the resident's physician and the representative under CARE-05 and updates the service plan.
After any fall, staff first check the resident for injury and do not move a resident with suspected serious injury. Staff call 911 when needed, then notify the nurse and Administrator immediately.

The Administrator or nurse notifies the physician and the resident's representative as soon as the resident's condition is known, following the notification policy in the resident's contract (CON-02) and the process in CARE-05.
If the fall caused injury, the Administrator reports it to IDPH within 24 hours under INC-01 and documents the date, time and method of the report.
Staff complete a Fall Incident Report before the end of the shift. It records the circumstances, injuries, witnesses, footwear, environment and actions taken.

Within 72 hours of any fall, the nurse and service plan team review the cause and revise fall interventions. A significant change in condition triggers a new comprehensive assessment by a physician, physician assistant or APRN under 210 ILCS 9/15.

The Administrator reassesses fall and skin risk at least annually with the comprehensive assessment, and at any more frequent interval IDPH sets by rule. The reassessment is documented in the resident record.
The Administrator reviews all fall and skin events each month, looks for trends by resident, time and location, and reports the results to the Quality Improvement Program (QI-01).
On request, the resident or representative is given a copy of the latest assessment, any supplemental establishment assessment and the service plan (210 ILCS 9/15).
All staff are trained on fall prevention, safe transfers and skin observation at orientation and at least annually (PER-06).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures assessments are completed, decides on admission or non-retention when a stage 3 or 4 ulcer needs treatment, makes the 24-hour IDPH report of a fall with injury, and reviews trends.
Reviews assessments, performs skin checks and wound observation, notifies the physician, and updates the service plan.
Follow service plan interventions, observe skin during care, report falls and skin changes, and complete incident reports.
Inspects for and corrects fall hazards and documents the work.
Take part in service plan decisions and report any concerns about falls or skin.

documentation: Physician, physician assistant or APRN comprehensive assessment and annual reassessments
Admission Skin Check form and subsequent skin observations
Service plan showing fall and skin risk and interventions
Fall Incident Reports and post-fall service plan reviews
Copy and date of any 24-hour IDPH report (INC-01)
Physician and representative notification records
Maintenance Log of hazard inspections
Monthly fall and skin trend report to QI-01

policies.category: Subpart D – Resident Care and Services (§ 295.4000–295.4060)
policies.title: Hospice and Home Health Coordination; Death of a Resident
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment – Administrator, nurse, direct care staff and business office
policies.purpose: To allow a terminally ill resident to remain in the establishment when hospice care is properly coordinated, and to handle a resident's death, notifications, funds and refunds with dignity and as the contract requires.
policies.policy: A terminally ill resident may stay at [AGENCY NAME] when hospice services are coordinated by a licensed hospice or a licensed home health professional and the resident, the representative, the hospice or home health provider and [AGENCY NAME] all agree (77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000(f)). The service plan is revised to incorporate the hospice plan of care (210 ILCS 9/15). If a party withdraws agreement, or [AGENCY NAME] can no longer provide or secure the services needed, the Administrator follows RES-03 and TERM-01. When a resident dies, [AGENCY NAME] follows the notification policy stated in the resident's contract under 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2030. Resident funds, deposits and refunds are settled under the contract's refund policy.

definitions.definition: A licensed hospice program that provides comfort-focused care to a terminally ill resident under a plan of care.
A licensed home health agency or licensed professional who coordinates the resident's care at the establishment.
The written plan developed by the hospice team that describes the resident's care, services and goals.
The emergency and relative notification policy that the establishment contract must contain under 295.2030(b).

procedures: When a resident, representative or physician requests hospice or end-of-life care in the establishment, the Administrator meets with the resident and representative within two business days to explain what [AGENCY NAME] can and cannot provide.
The Administrator confirms that the hospice or home health provider is licensed and obtains its name, license information and 24-hour contact number. Verification is recorded in the resident record.

The Administrator confirms that [AGENCY NAME] has staff of appropriate number and skill, and can provide or secure the needed services, as required by 295.2000. If not, the Administrator documents the gap and follows RES-03 and TERM-01.
The resident, representative, hospice or home health provider and Administrator sign a written agreement to the hospice arrangement. The agreement is filed in the resident record.

Within three business days of receiving the hospice plan of care, the service plan team revises the service plan to incorporate it. The plan states who does what: hospice staff, [AGENCY NAME] staff or others arranged with the resident's consent.
The nurse and the hospice case manager agree on a communication schedule. Direct care staff are told which hospice tasks they may perform and which are reserved for hospice or licensed personnel.
Medication handling for hospice residents follows MED-01 and MED-02. Staff do not give any medication that is outside their role or training.

The nurse or Administrator reviews the service plan with the hospice team whenever the resident's condition changes and at least at each hospice plan of care review. Changes are signed by the resident or representative.
Staff report changes in condition to the nurse. The nurse notifies the hospice and, as appropriate, the physician and representative, under CARE-05.

The Administrator reassesses at each change whether the establishment can still meet the resident's needs. If it cannot, the Administrator discusses relocation options with the resident, representative and hospice and follows TERM-01 notice requirements.

When a resident dies, staff on duty call the hospice (if enrolled) or 911 as the situation requires, and notify the Administrator immediately. The Administrator or nurse notifies the coroner or medical examiner when Illinois law requires.

The Administrator or designee notifies the representative and the persons named in the resident's contract, in the order and by the method set out in the contract notification policy (CON-02). Each call is recorded with the date, time and name of the person reached.
If the death was unexpected or involved an accident, abuse or neglect allegation, or a serious incident, the Administrator reports to IDPH within 24 hours under INC-01.

Staff treat the resident's body with respect and protect the privacy of other residents. Release of the body follows the wishes of the representative or the funeral home named by the family, and is documented.
